definition_zh: 咖啡；咖啡豆；咖啡色
definition_en: a hot drink made from roasted beans; the beans themselves
core_image: 一只冒着热气的杯子，深色的液体上有细细的白汽
scene: 冬天的早晨，爸爸端着热腾腾的杯子走进厨房。 Dad drinks a cup of coffee before going to work.
sceneCN: 这里 coffee 是「咖啡」（第 1 个义项：用咖啡豆冲泡的热饮）；句意是爸爸上班前喝一杯咖啡。

derivatives.zh: 由 coffee 加 house 构成，义为「咖啡馆」
源自法语，义为「咖啡馆；小餐馆」

senses.title: The hot drink
senses.definition: a hot brown drink made from roasted and ground beans
senses.definitionCN: 用烘烤研磨的豆子冲出的棕色热饮
senses.example: Hot coffee smells best on a cold morning.
senses.exampleCN: 冷天早晨的热咖啡闻起来最香。
senses.why: Boiling water poured on ground roasted beans gives a dark drink that wakes the body up.
senses.whyCN: 沸水冲过烘焙研磨的豆子，便得到提神的深色饮品。

senses.title: The beans or powder
senses.definition: the roasted beans or the powder made from them
senses.definitionCN: 烘焙过的豆子或研磨成的粉
senses.example: Grandma buys coffee beans from the southern farm.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶从南方农场买咖啡豆。
senses.why: The drink is named after the stuff it comes from, so beans and powder share the name.
senses.whyCN: 饮品以原料得名，豆子与粉便共享这个名字。

senses.title: A cup of coffee as a social event
senses.definition: an occasion of sitting together and drinking coffee
senses.definitionCN: 坐在一起喝咖啡的场合
senses.example: Let's have a coffee after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛结束后我们去喝杯咖啡吧。
senses.why: The drink became so friendly that the cup turned into an appointment.
senses.whyCN: 这种饮品太有社交气质，一杯咖啡便成了一场约会。

intro.en: Coffee crossed the world in a cup: from Ethiopia through Arabia and Turkey into Europe.
intro.cn: 咖啡装在杯子里跨越世界：从埃塞俄比亚经阿拉伯、土耳其进入欧洲。

items.en: Arabic qahwah first named the wine-like dark drink.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 qahwah 最初指这种像酒一样的深色饮品。

items.en: Turkish kahve passed the word north-west with the drink itself.
items.cn: 土耳其语 kahve 带着这种饮品把词传向西北。

items.en: Italian caffe softened the sound for European ears.
items.cn: 意大利语 caffe 让发音更柔和，以适应欧洲人的耳朵。

items.en: English took coffee in the seventeenth century when coffeehouses spread.
items.cn: 十七世纪咖啡馆盛行时，英语借入了 coffee。

items.en: Modern English added coffee shop, coffee break and instant coffee.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了 coffee shop、coffee break、instant coffee 等词。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects drink words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收饮品类词。

entries.definition: A place that serves coffee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咖啡馆」，由 coffee 加 house 构成。

entries.definition: A hard sweet made from sugar and butter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「太妃糖」，拼写与 coffee 相近但词源无关。

entries.definition: A small restaurant serving coffee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咖啡馆」，源自同一法语链条。

entries.definition: A hot drink made from dried leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「茶」，用干茶叶冲泡。

entries.definition: A hot drink made from cacao powder.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可可」，用可可粉冲泡。

entries.definition: A small strong cup of coffee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浓缩咖啡」，量小而浓。

normalIntro.en: Remember coffee through its long journey and its warm cup.
normalIntro.cn: 沿着漫长的旅程与温暖的杯子记忆 coffee。

normal.en: coffee travelled from Arabic qahwah to English.
normal.cn: coffee 从阿拉伯语 qahwah 一路走到英语。

normal.en: black coffee has no milk in it.
normal.cn: black coffee 不加奶。

normal.en: instant coffee mixes fast in hot water.
normal.cn: instant coffee 在热水里很快化开。

normal.en: a coffee break is a short rest at work.
normal.cn: coffee break 是工作间隙的小憩。

normal.en: the plural coffees means cups of it.
normal.cn: coffees 指一杯杯咖啡。

abstract.en: Hear the soft drip of the coffee pot early in the morning.
abstract.cn: 听清晨咖啡壶轻轻的滴答声。

abstract.en: Feel the warm cup pass from one hand to a friend's.
abstract.cn: 感受暖杯从一只手递到朋友手里。

abstract.en: See two friends talking till the cups run empty.
abstract.cn: 想象两位朋友聊到杯底见空。

examples.en: Mom made three coffees for the guests last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚妈妈为客人做了三杯咖啡。

examples.en: The coffee shop near school sells milk tea too.
examples.cn: 学校附近的咖啡店也卖奶茶。

examples.en: Two spoons of coffee powder made the kitchen smell rich.
examples.cn: 两勺咖啡粉让厨房满是香气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「咖啡」——苦香扑鼻，人们喝了都说「咖啡！咖啡！」，coffee 就是这杯深色热饮。

root: 阿拉伯语 qahwah（深色饮品）→ 土耳其语 kahve → 意大利语 caffe → 十七世纪英语 coffee；同源词有 cafe（咖啡馆），派生词有 coffeehouse（咖啡馆）。

sensesIntro.en: Coffee names the drink, the beans and the friendly break it creates.
sensesIntro.cn: coffee 指饮品、豆子，也指它带来的社交时光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warm dark steam rising from a small cup
core.cn: 核心意象：小杯中升起温热的深色蒸汽

branches.en: The hot brown drink
branches.cn: 棕色热饮

branches.en: The beans and powder
branches.cn: 豆子与咖啡粉

branches.en: The friendly cup
branches.cn: 社交的一杯

branches.en: Shops and breaks
branches.cn: 咖啡馆与茶歇

branches.en: Farms far to the south
branches.cn: 远在南方的农场

intro.en: Coffee builds cozy compounds of cups and houses.
intro.cn: coffee 构造出杯子与屋子的温馨复合词。

latinIntro.en: Coffee is Arabic in origin, so Latin relatives are absent.
latinIntro.cn: coffee 源自阿拉伯语，没有拉丁同族词。

items.example: We ate lunch at the corner cafe.
items.exampleCN: 我们在街角小馆吃午饭。

items.meaning: strong coffee in a small cup
items.exampleCN: 一杯浓缩咖啡让他保持清醒。

items.meaning: a person making coffee in a cafe
items.example: The barista drew a heart on it.
items.exampleCN: 咖啡师在上面画了颗心。

definition_zh: 不喜欢；厌恶（动词或名词）
definition_en: to not like someone or something
core_image: 推开眼前食物的手
scene: 面对一盘生拌菜。 I dislike raw onions, but my dad loves them.
sceneCN: 这里 dislike 是「不喜欢」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我不喜欢生洋葱，但爸爸很喜欢。

derivatives.zh: dislike 的词基，义为「喜欢」
义为「喜好」
少用，义为「令人讨厌的」

senses.title: To feel that something is unpleasant
senses.definition: to find someone or something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某人或某物让人不舒服
senses.example: She dislikes getting up early on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 她不喜欢周末早起。
senses.why: Like meant to please; dis- cancels the pleasing feeling.
senses.whyCN: like 本义是「使愉悦」，dis- 取消这份愉悦感。

senses.title: A feeling of not liking
senses.definition: the feeling of not liking something
senses.definitionCN: 不喜欢的感觉
senses.example: He has a strong dislike of horror films.
senses.exampleCN: 他对恐怖片很反感。
senses.why: The cancelled pleasure becomes a lasting feeling.
senses.whyCN: 被取消的愉悦沉淀成一种持续的感觉。

intro.en: Dislike is like wearing the negative dis-.
intro.cn: dislike 是 like 加否定前缀 dis-。

items.en: Old English gelic meant similar or pleasing.
items.cn: 古英语 gelic 意为相似的、令人愉悦的。

items.en: Like grew into a verb meaning to please, then to enjoy.
items.cn: 中古英语 like 先指取悦，后指喜爱。

items.en: The prefix dis- built dislike in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪加 dis- 构成 dislike。

items.en: The verb is common; the noun names a fixed feeling.
items.cn: 动词用法常见，名词指固定的反感。

items.en: Likes and dislikes together describe a person's tastes.
items.cn: likes and dislikes 合指一个人的好恶。

note.en: These words share the like root or the feeling field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 like 词根，或属于情感义场。

entries.definition: verb: to enjoy something
entries.definitionCN: 动词：喜欢

entries.definition: noun: a taste for something
entries.definitionCN: 名词：喜好

entries.definition: adverb: in the same way
entries.definitionCN: 副词：同样地

entries.definition: adjective: probable
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：可能的

entries.definition: adjective: similar
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：相似的

entries.definition: to dislike strongly
entries.definitionCN: 讨厌；憎恨

entries.definition: to keep away from
entries.definitionCN: 避开

entries.definition: to find something unbearable
entries.definitionCN: 受不了

entries.definition: to get pleasure from
entries.definitionCN: 享受（反义方向）

entries.definition: to feel like having
entries.definitionCN: 想要（反义方向）

normalIntro.en: Split it: dis- (not) + like.
normalIntro.cn: 拆开记忆：dis-（不）+ like（喜欢）。

normal.en: dislike = dis + like.
normal.cn: dislike 由 dis 加 like 构成。

normal.en: dislike is followed by doing: dislike doing.
normal.cn: dislike 后接动名词：dislike doing。

normal.en: have a dislike of something is the noun pattern.
normal.cn: have a dislike of sth 是名词句型。

normal.en: likes and dislikes means tastes.
normal.cn: likes and dislikes 指好恶。

normal.en: dislike is softer than hate.
normal.cn: dislike 比 hate 语气轻。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a plate away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把盘子推开。

abstract.en: Hear a small sigh at the smell.
abstract.cn: 闻到味道时的一声轻叹。

abstract.en: Feel the shoulders turning sideways.
abstract.cn: 体会肩膀悄悄转开的动作。

examples.en: I dislike doing homework with the TV on.
examples.cn: 我不喜欢开着电视写作业。

examples.en: Most people dislike being laughed at.
examples.cn: 大多数人不喜欢被嘲笑。

examples.en: My dislike of maths is fading because my teacher is fun.
examples.cn: 因为老师很有趣，我对数学的反感在消退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟斯拉伊克」——弟弟一赖床就说不喜欢早起

root: 来自 dislike，dis-（不）+ like（喜欢）；like 源自古英语 gelic（相似的、令人愉悦的）。

sensesIntro.en: Dislike cancels the pleasing feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: dislike 取消那份「愉悦」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a plate away
core.cn: 核心意象：推开盘子的手

branches.en: The pushed-away thing
branches.cn: 被推开的事物

branches.en: The lasting feeling
branches.cn: 沉淀的反感

branches.en: From act to feeling
branches.cn: 从动作到感受

branches.en: Monday morning alarms
branches.cn: 周一早晨的闹钟

branches.en: A list of dislikes
branches.cn: 一张反感清单

intro.en: Dislike = dis- + like.
intro.cn: dislike 由 dis- 加 like 构成。

latinIntro.en: The root is Old English gelic, pleasing.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是古英语 gelic（令人愉悦的）。

definition_zh: 火；火灾；炉火；炮火；热情；开火；解雇；点火
definition_en: burning with flames and light, a burning that destroys, the heat of a hearth, or gunshots; as verbs, to shoot, dismiss or set alight
core_image: 一堆跳动的橙色火焰，既照亮又吞噬
scene: 冬夜的山屋里，柴火噼啪作响映红了围坐者的脸。 We sat around the fire and told stories till midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 fire 是名词，指「炉火、篝火」，对应第 3 个义项；句为我们围炉讲故事直到半夜。

derivatives.zh: 消防员（fire 与 man 复合，指灭火之人）
消防员（fire 与 fighter 复合，指与火搏斗之人）
被解雇的；烧制的（fire 的过去分词，指被辞退或经窑烧的）

senses.title: Burning with flames
senses.definition: the state of burning that produces light and heat
senses.definitionCN: 产生光与热的燃烧状态
senses.example: The hut went up in flames when a fire started in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房起火，小屋被火焰吞噬。
senses.why: Light, heat and eating wood: the first picture of fire is consumption made visible.
senses.whyCN: 光、热与吞食木柴：火焰最初的画面即「可见的吞噬」。

senses.title: A destructive burning
senses.definition: an uncontrolled burning that destroys property
senses.definitionCN: 失去控制、摧毁财物的燃烧
senses.example: The factory fire destroyed three workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂火灾烧毁了三间车间。
senses.why: When fire escapes its hearth it turns from servant to enemy.
senses.whyCN: 火焰一旦脱离炉膛，便从仆从变为敌人。

senses.title: A hearth or campfire
senses.definition: a controlled fire used for warmth, cooking or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 用于取暖、做饭或仪式的受控之火
senses.example: They cooked supper over an open fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在篝火上做晚饭。
senses.why: Tamed fire gathers people around it: warmth is social.
senses.whyCN: 被驯服的火把人聚拢：温暖具有社交性。

senses.title: Gunshots
senses.definition: the shots fired from guns
senses.definitionCN: 枪炮射出的弹药
senses.example: The soldiers came under heavy fire.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们遭到猛烈炮火袭击。
senses.why: Guns eject fire, so the discharge of weapons borrows the flame.
senses.whyCN: 枪炮喷吐火焰，于是武器的发射借用了火之名。

senses.title: Strong emotion or energy
senses.definition: intense emotion, energy or inspiration
senses.definitionCN: 强烈的情绪、干劲或灵感
senses.example: Her speech was full of fire.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演讲充满激情。
senses.why: Burning inside the body is indistinguishable from burning in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 体内之烧与心中之烧在语言上难分彼此。

senses.title: To dismiss from a job
senses.definition: to make someone leave their job
senses.definitionCN: 使某人离开工作岗位
senses.example: He was fired for missing deadlines.
senses.exampleCN: 他因屡屡误期被解雇。
senses.why: The old way of ending work was a payment: firing was settling the account.
senses.whyCN: 旧时终止雇佣的方式是结清款项：解雇即结账。

intro.en: Fire is a native Germanic word of the hearth and the flame, older than writing, with cousins across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: fire 是属于炉膛与火焰的日耳曼本族词，比文字更古老，在各日耳曼语言中都有同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed root fur- meant 'fire'; German Feuer and Dutch vuur are cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fur- 意为「火」；德语 Feuer 与荷兰语 vuur 是同族词。

items.en: Old English fyr meant 'fire', central to life, cooking and belief.
items.cn: 古英语 fyr 意为「火」，是生活、烹饪与信仰的中心。

items.en: Middle English fir covered hearth fires and destructive burns alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 fir 兼指炉火与灾害之火。

items.en: Guns made fire the word for gunfire and for shooting.
items.cn: 枪炮使 fire 成为炮火与射击的用词。

items.en: Industrial English added the dismissal sense, from settling an account at the end of work.
items.cn: 近代英语又添解雇义，源于雇佣终结时的结清。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fi- shape or the hearth root; near-meaning words burn in the same field.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fi- 字形或炉火词根；近义组在同一燃烧义场。

entries.definition: to cook in hot oil; sound-alike but a different root
entries.definitionCN: 用油炸；音近而词根不同

entries.definition: to employ; fire's workplace opposite
entries.definitionCN: 雇用；fire 在职场的反义词

entries.definition: violent anger; close in sound but unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 暴怒；音近而无关

entries.definition: the visible burning gas of a fire
entries.definitionCN: 火焰；明火

entries.definition: a large, bright fire
entries.definitionCN: 大火；烈火

entries.definition: a huge destructive fire
entries.definitionCN: 火海；大灾难之火

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the hearth and the modern verb uses.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自炉火意象与现代动词用法的记忆抓手。

normal.en: catch fire means flames have begun.
normal.cn: catch fire 表示火已烧起来。

normal.en: fire a gun and fire an employee share one verb: both are sudden endings.
normal.cn: fire a gun 与 fire an employee 共用一动词：都是突然的终结。

normal.en: German Feuer is the same word: the hearth family is old.
normal.cn: 德语 Feuer 与之同词：炉火词族古老。

normal.en: full of fire means burning with energy.
normal.cn: full of fire 表示充满干劲。

normal.en: open fire means to start shooting.
normal.cn: open fire 表示开始射击。

abstract.en: Fire is energy that has found a body to wear.
abstract.cn: 火是找到了躯壳的能量。

abstract.en: Anger is a house fire of the mind: it starts small and spreads.
abstract.cn: 愤怒是心灵的家宅之火：起于微末，蔓延成灾。

abstract.en: Dismissal is a door that burns on the way out.
abstract.cn: 解雇是一扇离开时还在燃烧的门。

examples.en: Smoke poured from the burning building before the fire brigade arrived.
examples.cn: 消防队赶到前，浓烟已从起火大楼涌出。

examples.en: The company fired three managers last month.
examples.cn: 公司上个月解雇了三名经理。

examples.en: The crowd was fired up by the band's last song.
examples.cn: 乐队的最后一首歌点燃了全场观众的热情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法爷」—— 火苗乱窜，法爷喊一声「法爷水来也」→ fire 火

root: 日耳曼本族词，出自古英语 fyr「火」，上溯重构词根 fur-；德语 Feuer、荷兰语 vuur 同族；核心是「燃烧之光与热」。

sensesIntro.en: From the flame outward to disasters, hearths, gunfire, passion and dismissal.
sensesIntro.cn: 从火焰出发，扩展到火灾、炉火、炮火、激情与解雇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: orange flames that light the dark and eat their fuel.
core.cn: 核心意象：照亮黑暗并吞噬燃料的橙色火焰。

branches.en: THE FLAME: burning itself.
branches.cn: 火焰：燃烧本身。

branches.en: THE DISASTER: fire out of control.
branches.cn: 灾害：失控之火。

branches.en: THE HEARTH: fire tamed for warmth.
branches.cn: 炉火：被驯服的暖。

branches.en: THE GUNFIRE: weapons that spit flame.
branches.cn: 炮火：喷吐火焰的武器。

branches.en: THE BURN WITHIN: passion, and the job that ends.
branches.cn: 内在之烧：激情，与被终止的职位。

intro.en: Fire compounds eagerly: firefighter, fireplace, firearm and more.
intro.cn: fire 极易复合构词：firefighter、fireplace、firearm 等。

latinIntro.en: Latin used ignis 'fire', root of ignite, unrelated to the Germanic fire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ignis「火」（ignite 的词根），与日耳曼的 fire 无关。

items.example: The bricks were fired at noon.
The school held a fire drill.

definition_zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；急奔；（磨坊）水道
definition_en: a competition to see who is fastest; a contest between people or groups; a group of people sharing ancestry; to move very fast; a channel of water leading to a mill
core_image: 傍晚的跑道上，几名选手同时冲过起跑线
scene: 傍晚的跑道上，发令枪响后几名选手同时冲出起跑线。 He won the final race by less than a second.
sceneCN: 这里 race 是「赛跑、竞速比赛」（第 1 个义项：比谁跑得快的比赛）；句意为他以不到一秒的优势赢下了最后一场比赛。画面里可留意：起点线、发令枪、几乎并排的身影。

pos.zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；（磨坊）水道
急速行进；参赛；使拼命跑

derivatives.zh: race 加 -er，指参赛者或赛车
race 加 -ing，指赛跑、赛车等竞技活动
race 加 -ial，指与种族有关的
race 加 -ist，指持种族歧视观点的

senses.title: A competition of speed
senses.definition: a contest to find who or what is fastest
senses.definitionCN: 比出谁或什么最快的一种竞赛
senses.example: He won the hundred-metre race.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢下了百米赛跑。
senses.why: The contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush or a run, so the word began as the movement itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛义来自一个古老的北方词，意为「急冲、奔跑」，所以这个词最初指的就是那股奔跑。

senses.title: A contest between people or groups
senses.definition: a situation in which people or groups try to be first to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体争相抢先达到某个目标的情形
senses.example: The race for the contract ended in a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 争取这份合同的竞争以平局收场。
senses.why: Once a race was a run toward a line, any struggle to arrive first could be called a race, even without running.
senses.whyCN: 当 race 指朝终点线奔跑之后，任何「抢在前头」的争夺都可以叫 race，即使根本不用跑。

senses.title: A group sharing ancestry
senses.definition: a group of people regarded as sharing ancestry and physical features, a term used with care
senses.definitionCN: 被视为共享血统与外貌特征的一群人，此词使用时须谨慎
senses.example: People of every race took part in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 各种族的人都参加了这项调查。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source, an Italian word for kind or breed, and its scientific status has been much debated.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同，出自一个意为「种类、品种」的意大利语词，其科学地位一直备受争议。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: to move at great speed, often in a hurry or in competition
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度移动，常带匆忙或竞争意味
senses.example: She raced to catch the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 她飞奔去赶末班车。
senses.why: Since the word first named a rush, the verb simply describes the act of rushing, with or without a contest.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词最初指一股急冲，动词就只是描述急冲这一动作，无论有没有比赛。

senses.title: A channel of water
senses.definition: a fast current of water, especially one made to drive a mill wheel
senses.definitionCN: 流速较快的水道，尤指为驱动磨坊水轮而开的渠道
senses.example: The old mill still stands beside the race.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老磨坊仍然立在水道旁边。
senses.why: Water rushing through a narrow channel moves like a runner, so the old sense of a rush survived in the mill race.
senses.whyCN: 水冲过窄渠时像奔跑者一样急行，于是「急冲」这一古老意思在磨坊水道里保留下来。

intro.en: Race is really two words: the contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush, while the ancestry sense comes through French and Italian from a word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: race 实际上是两个词：比赛义来自古老的北方词「急冲」，而种族义经法语与意大利语来自一个来源不确定的词。

items.en: Ras meant a running or a rush, and it entered northern English with the sense of swift movement.
items.cn: ras 意为奔跑、急冲，带着快速运动的意思进入英格兰北部英语。

items.en: Middle English race named a run or a course, and from that a contest of speed.
items.cn: 中古英语的 race 指一次奔跑或一段跑道，由此生出速度竞赛之义。

items.en: A separate French word razza, of uncertain origin, meant a breed or a kind, especially of animals.
items.cn: 另一个来源不确定的法语词 razza 意为品种或种类，尤指动物的品种。

items.en: English applied the breed sense to groups of people, a use that later became scientifically and socially disputed.
items.cn: 英语把「品种」义用到人群上，这一用法后来在科学与社会层面都引发争议。

items.en: Modern English keeps both words: race as a contest and race as a category of people, plus the mill race of flowing water.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两个词：作为竞赛的 race、作为人群类别的 race，以及指流水渠道的磨坊 race。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the word; the near-meaning group gathers words for contests, speed and ancestry.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词构成的形式；近义组收表示竞赛、速度与血统的词。

entries.definition: A person or vehicle that takes part in races.
entries.definitionCN: 参加比赛的人或车辆。

entries.definition: The sport of competing for speed.
entries.definitionCN: 比速度的竞技运动。

entries.definition: Connected with a group sharing ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享血统的群体有关的。

entries.definition: Someone who treats people unequally because of their group.
entries.definitionCN: 因所属群体而区别对待他人的人。

entries.definition: A competition in which people try to win.
entries.definitionCN: 人们争胜的比赛。

entries.definition: The activity of trying to do better than others.
entries.definitionCN: 力图胜过他人的活动。

entries.definition: To run at top speed for a short distance.
entries.definitionCN: 短距离全速奔跑。

entries.definition: Belonging to a group with shared culture and origin.
entries.definitionCN: 属于共享文化与来源的群体。

normalIntro.en: The contest sense grew from a word for a rush of movement, and the ancestry sense grew from a word for breed; English keeps both under one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 比赛义从表示「急冲」的词生长出来，种族义从表示「品种」的词生长出来；英语把两者放在同一个拼写之下。

normal.en: Race as a contest and race as a category of people have different origins that happen to share one spelling.
normal.cn: 作为竞赛的 race 与作为人群类别的 race 来源不同，只是碰巧共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: A race against time is a race with no competitor but the clock.
normal.cn: race against time 是没有对手、只与时钟赛跑的比赛。

normal.en: Racer, racing and racial all come from the same short word with different endings.
normal.cn: racer、racing、racial 都是同一个短词加上不同词尾。

normal.en: A mill race is water rushing through a channel, which shows how old the sense of a rush really is.
normal.cn: mill race 指冲过渠道的水，可见「急冲」这一古老意思有多深。

normal.en: The human race uses race in the broad sense of all people together, not in the sense of a category.
normal.cn: the human race 用的是「全人类」这一宽泛义，而不是「某一类别」义。

abstract.en: Sorting people into races says more about the sorter than about the people being sorted.
abstract.cn: 把人分成种族，更多说明分类者本身，而不是被分类的人。

abstract.en: A race is exciting because everyone agrees on the same finish line, which is also why disagreements about the line are so bitter.
abstract.cn: 比赛令人兴奋，因为大家认同同一条终点线，这也正是关于终点线的分歧如此激烈的原因。

abstract.en: Speed is easy to measure and easy to admire, which is why so much of modern life is arranged as a race.
abstract.cn: 速度容易测量，也容易赞美，所以现代生活有很大一部分被安排成一场比赛。

examples.en: She came second in the school race.
examples.cn: 她在学校赛跑中得了第二。

examples.en: The two companies are in a race to launch first.
examples.cn: 两家公司在争抢谁先发布。

examples.en: He raced down the stairs when he heard the alarm.
examples.cn: 听到警报，他飞奔下楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐丝」——像一根锐利的丝线划过终点，速度极快，记住 race 是赛跑、竞赛。

root: 比赛义源于古诺斯语 ras（奔跑、急冲）；种族义经法语与意大利语来自 razza（品种，来源不确定）；两词在英语中同形。同族有 racer、racing、racial。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rush; one branch runs from rush to contest, the other from breed to ancestry, and a third survives in the channel of a mill.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「急冲」；一条支线从急冲走到竞赛，另一条从品种走到血统，还有一条留在磨坊的水道里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: runners leaving the start line together on an evening track.
core.cn: 核心意象：傍晚跑道上同时冲出起跑线的选手。

branches.en: a gun fired beside a track
branches.cn: 跑道旁打响的发令枪

branches.en: two firms chasing one contract
branches.cn: 两家公司争抢同一份合同

branches.en: a form asking for ancestry
branches.cn: 要求填写血统的表格

branches.en: feet taking the stairs three at a time
branches.cn: 一步三级地冲下楼梯

branches.en: the same rush, once on legs and once in a mill channel
branches.cn: 同一种急冲，一次靠双腿，一次在磨坊渠道里

intro.en: The contest word is native and northern, the ancestry word came through French and Italian, and English adds its usual endings to both.
intro.cn: 表示竞赛的词是本族词，来自北方；表示血统的词经法语和意大利语传来；英语给两者加上了惯用的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for either word.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个来源都没有可靠的拉丁语出处记录。

definition_zh: 收集；搜集；聚集；领取
definition_en: to bring things or people together from different places, often carefully and one by one
core_image: 把散在各处的东西一件件拢到自己面前
scene: 邮票散落在桌子各处，哥哥把它们一张张夹进册子。 My brother began to collect stamps from all over the world last year.
sceneCN: 这里 collect 是「收集」（第 1 个义项：把东西聚拢）；句意是哥哥从去年开始收集世界各地的邮票。

derivatives.zh: 由 collect 加 -ion 构成，义为「收集品；收藏；采集」
由 collect 加 -or 构成，义为「收集者；收藏家」
由 collect 加 -ive 构成，义为「集体的；共同的」

senses.title: To bring things together
senses.definition: to gather things from different places and keep them together
senses.definitionCN: 把散在不同地方的东西聚拢到一起保存
senses.example: The class began to collect old books for the library.
senses.exampleCN: 全班开始为图书馆收集旧书。
senses.why: The prefix col- means together and lect means gather, so the word pictures pulling things into one pile.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 col- 表示「一起」，lect 表示「聚集」，词义就是把东西拉到一堆。

senses.title: To gather people together
senses.definition: to bring people together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把人聚集到同一个地方
senses.example: The teacher collected the students in the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把学生集合在操场上。
senses.why: Gathering works for people as well as things, so the word widened to groups of persons.
senses.whyCN: 聚集既能用于物也能用于人，词义便扩展到人群。

senses.title: To go and get something waiting for you
senses.definition: to go somewhere and take away something or someone kept for you
senses.definitionCN: 去某个地方把为你保管的东西或人带走
senses.example: Please collect your test papers at the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 请到前台领取你们的试卷。
senses.why: What has been gathered is kept somewhere, and taking it back is the last step of collecting.
senses.whyCN: 被聚拢的东西会被保管在某处，取回它就是收集的最后一步。

senses.title: To get money or rent
senses.definition: to obtain money that is owed or given, often for a group
senses.definitionCN: 把欠的或捐的钱收上来
senses.example: Students collect money for the sports meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们为运动会筹款。
senses.why: Money also needs to be brought together from many people, so the same verb fits.
senses.whyCN: 钱也需要从许多人那里聚到一起，同一个动词便沿用下来。

senses.title: To calm oneself
senses.definition: to calm yourself and focus before doing something hard
senses.definitionCN: 在做事之前让自己平静下来、集中精神
senses.example: She took a deep breath to collect herself before the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲前她深呼吸让自己镇定下来。
senses.why: Collecting your thoughts is like collecting papers: everything scattered is put in order.
senses.whyCN: 整理思绪就像收试卷：把散乱的东西归置整齐。

intro.en: Collect means to gather together, built on Latin roots.
intro.cn: collect 的意思是「聚到一起」，由拉丁词根搭成。

items.en: Latin legere meant to gather or pick out, and com- added the idea of together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为收集、挑选，前缀 com- 加上了「一起」的意思。

items.en: Latin colligere meant to gather together into one.
items.cn: 拉丁语 colligere 意为聚拢到一处。

items.en: Old French collecter and collecte passed the gathering idea on.
items.cn: 古法语 collecter、collecte 把「聚集」的意思传了下来。

items.en: Middle English collecten first named gathering money in church.
items.cn: 中古英语 collecten 最初指在教堂里募捐收钱。

items.en: Modern English collect grew into study, rubbish, tickets and people.
items.cn: 现代英语 collect 的用法扩展到收藏、垃圾、取票和集合人群。

note.en: The first group collects words with the same root lect; the second collects words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词根 lect 的词，第二组收近义词。

entries.definition: A group of things gathered together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收藏品；收集」，是 collect 的名词形式。

entries.definition: A person who collects things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收藏家；收集者」，与 collect 同根。

entries.definition: To choose someone by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选举」，含同一词根 lect（挑选）。

entries.definition: To choose from several things.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挑选」，同根词。

entries.definition: To bring things or people together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「聚集；收集」，与 collect 意思相近但更口语。

entries.definition: To gather people or parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「集合；装配」，较正式。

entries.definition: To collect more and more over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积累」，强调逐渐变多。

normalIntro.en: Remember collect through its Latin parts and its everyday jobs.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁词根与日常用途两个角度记 collect。

normal.en: col- means together and -lect means gather.
normal.cn: col- 表示一起，-lect 表示聚集。

normal.en: select, elect and collect share the root.
normal.cn: select、elect 和 collect 同词根。

normal.en: Rubbish trucks collect rubbish every morning.
normal.cn: 垃圾车每天早上收垃圾。

normal.en: Collect your ticket before boarding the train.
normal.cn: 上火车前先取票。

normal.en: A stamp collector keeps stamps in an album.
normal.cn: 集邮者把邮票收在册子里。

abstract.en: Picture scattered leaves being swept into one pile.
abstract.cn: 想象散落的树叶被扫成一堆。

abstract.en: See hands from many places placing coins in one box.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手把硬币放进同一个箱子。

abstract.en: Feel a deep breath pulling your thoughts into order.
abstract.cn: 感觉一次深呼吸把思绪理顺。

examples.en: We collect waste paper every Friday to keep the school clean.
examples.cn: 每周五我们都收集废纸保持校园整洁。

examples.en: Remember to collect your new uniform from the office.
examples.cn: 记得去办公室领取你的新校服。

examples.en: Playing the piano helps her collect her thoughts.
examples.cn: 弹钢琴帮助她集中思绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扩来摭」——把散落四边的东西都「扩来摭」到一起，collect 就是收集。

root: 拉丁语 com-（一起）+ legere（收集、挑选）→ colligere（聚拢）→ 古法语 collecte → 现代英语 collect；同族词有 select（挑选）、elect（选举）、collection（收藏）等。

sensesIntro.en: Collect starts with gathering things and grows to people, money and a calm mind.
sensesIntro.cn: collect 从收集物品出发，扩展到集合人群、收钱与镇定心神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pulling scattered things into one place
core.cn: 核心意象：把散落的东西拢到一处

branches.en: Stamps, books and rubbish
branches.cn: 邮票、旧书与垃圾

branches.en: Students lined up on the playground
branches.cn: 操场上集合的学生

branches.en: Tickets waiting at the desk
branches.cn: 前台等着领取的票

branches.en: Money for the sports meeting
branches.cn: 运动会的筹款

branches.en: Scattered thoughts put in order
branches.cn: 散乱思绪被理顺

intro.en: Collect sits in a big family built on the Latin root lect.
intro.cn: collect 属于以拉丁词根 lect 为核心的大词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root lect means to gather or choose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 lect 意为收集、挑选。

items.example: Her coin collection fills two boxes.
items.exampleCN: 她的硬币收藏装满两个盒子。

items.example: The collector showed his old maps.
items.exampleCN: 收藏家展示了他收藏的旧地图。

items.example: Select the answer you think is right.
items.exampleCN: 选出你认为正确的答案。

items.example: We elect a class monitor every term.
items.exampleCN: 我们每学期选一次班长。

items.example: I cannot recollect his phone number.
items.exampleCN: 我记不起他的电话号码了。

items.example: The professor gave a lecture on birds.
items.exampleCN: 教授做了一场关于鸟类的讲座。

definition_zh: 纪录片；纪实的；文献的
definition_en: a film or programme that gives facts about real people and events
core_image: 摄影机对准真实发生的现场
scene: 晚自习结束后，班里的投影幕布亮起，老师按下播放键。 The class watched a documentary about wild pandas.
sceneCN: 这里 documentary 是「纪录片」（第 1 个义项：讲真实事实的影片）；句意：全班观看了一部关于野生大熊猫的纪录片。

derivatives.zh: documentary 加表示者后缀构成，义为「纪录片制作人」
documentary 的基础词，义为「文件；文献」

senses.title: A film of real facts
senses.definition: a film or programme giving facts about real life
senses.definitionCN: 讲述真实生活事实的电影或节目
senses.example: The documentary follows whales across the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片追踪鲸鱼横渡大洋。
senses.why: The word is built on document: the film is treated as a moving paper of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 document 之上：影片被当作一页会动的证据纸。

senses.title: Based on written records
senses.definition: based on or using documents
senses.definitionCN: 基于文件或使用文献的
senses.example: The film used documentary evidence from the war.
senses.exampleCN: 影片引用了战争时期的书面证据。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the paper sense: proof still comes from documents.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留纸张义：证据仍来自文献。

intro.en: Documentary grew straight out of document, the paper that teaches.
intro.cn: documentary 直接从 document（教导人的纸张）中生长出来。

items.en: Latin documentum meant lesson, from docere to teach.
items.cn: 拉丁语 documentum 意为课程，来自 docere（教导）。

items.en: French document passed on the paper sense.
items.cn: 法语 document 传下了「文件」之义。

items.en: English document settled as written proof.
items.cn: 英语 document 定型为书面证据。

items.en: French film documentaire named factual films in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，法语 film documentaire 用来命名纪实影片。

items.en: English documentary became the standard word for factual film.
items.cn: 英语 documentary 成为纪实影片的标准用词。

note.en: These words sit near documentary in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 documentary 相邻。

entries.definition: written proof
entries.definitionCN: 文件

entries.definition: written guides or proof
entries.definitionCN: 文档

entries.definition: basic level, different root
entries.definitionCN: 初级的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a film of real events
entries.definitionCN: 纪实影片

entries.definition: an old cinema news film
entries.definitionCN: 新闻影片

entries.definition: a film of a real person's life
entries.definitionCN: 传记影片

normalIntro.en: Use the camera-on-fact picture and the document family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「镜头对准事实」的画面和 document 词族来记。

normal.en: watch a documentary is the common phrase in class.
normal.cn: watch a documentary 是课堂常见说法。

normal.en: documentary is document plus film.
normal.cn: documentary 就是 document 加影片。

normal.en: A nature documentary films real animals.
normal.cn: 自然纪录片拍摄真实动物。

normal.en: documentary evidence is written proof, not film.
normal.cn: documentary evidence 指书面证据而非影片。

normal.en: documentaries tell true stories without actors.
normal.cn: documentaries 讲真事，不用演员演戏。

abstract.en: Hear the soft hum of the camera following the herd.
abstract.cn: 听摄影机跟随兽群时轻微的嗡鸣。

abstract.en: See rain on the lens as the explorer walks on.
abstract.cn: 看雨点落在探险者前行镜头的镜片上。

abstract.en: Feel the quiet truth of a voice reading dates.
abstract.cn: 感受旁白念出年份时的静穆真实。

examples.en: The students made a short documentary about their town.
examples.cn: 学生们拍了一部关于家乡小镇的短片纪录片。

examples.en: A documentary about volcanoes is on tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚有一部关于火山的纪录片。

examples.en: She gave documentary proof of her studies abroad.
examples.cn: 她出示了海外学习的书面证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「到亏门缺」——纪录片拍到一半资金「到亏门缺」，只好如实记录空镜头

root: 来自拉丁语 documentum（课程）经 document（文件）派生；二十世纪初借法语 film documentaire 指「用事实说话」的影片。

sensesIntro.en: Documentary names factual films and, as an adjective, anything built on documents.
sensesIntro.cn: documentary 作名词指纪实影片，作形容词指基于文献的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lens pointed at real life
core.cn: 核心意象：摄影机对准真实发生的现场

branches.en: The film of real events
branches.cn: 拍真实事件的影片

branches.en: The proof from papers
branches.cn: 来自纸面的证据

branches.en: The quiet narration of facts
branches.cn: 平静陈述事实的旁白

branches.en: The archive shelf behind the film
branches.cn: 影片背后的档案架

branches.en: From paper proof to moving proof
branches.cn: 从纸面证据到动态证据

intro.en: Documentary is a document word with a film twist.
intro.cn: documentary 是 document 词族里带影片色彩的一员。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin docere, to teach.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 docere（教导）。

definition_zh: 在线的；联网的；网上的；在网上；联网地
definition_en: connected to or available through a computer network, especially the internet; as an adverb, by means of such a connection
core_image: 一根细线从桌上的机器伸向看不见的远方，屏幕随即亮起别人的声音
scene: 深夜的书房里只剩屏幕的光，桌角那根网线轻轻闪着小灯。 She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
sceneCN: 这里 online 是「在网上、联网地」（第 2 个义项：通过互联网进行某种活动）；句意是她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。画面是深夜的书房、亮着的屏幕与闪烁的网线指示灯。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「离开」的 off 与 line 复合，与 online 构成反义对，义为「离线的」
由 online 与 only 复合而成，义为「只在网上提供或经营的」

senses.title: Connected to a computer network
senses.definition: connected to a computer network or to the internet and able to exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 接入计算机网络或互联网，能够交换数据
senses.example: The printer is online, so the file went straight to paper.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机已联网，文件直接就印到了纸上。
senses.why: Line first named a wire or a telephone connection, so being on that line is literally being attached to the network.
senses.whyCN: line 最初指一根导线或一条电话线，所谓「在这条线上」就是实实在在接在网络里。

senses.title: By means of an internet connection
senses.definition: by using an internet connection rather than a physical place or a paper form
senses.definitionCN: 借助互联网连接，而不是通过实体场所或纸质表格
senses.example: She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。
senses.why: Once the line carries data, any action done through it can take the same word as an adverb of manner.
senses.whyCN: 当这条线传输的是数据，任何经由它完成的动作都能用同一个词作方式状语。

senses.title: Available or stored on the internet
senses.definition: existing, offered or stored on the internet, as opposed to a printed or physical version
senses.definitionCN: 存在于互联网上、在网上提供或保存的，与纸质或实体版本相对
senses.example: The journal moved its whole archive online last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家期刊去年把全部过刊搬到了网上。
senses.why: The adjective then moves from the connected machine to the thing that can only be reached through that connection.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词于是从「联网的机器」转到「只能通过网络抵达的内容」。

intro.en: Online joins the old noun line with the preposition on, and its modern life began with telephone wires before it passed to computer networks.
intro.cn: online 把古老的名词 line 与介词 on 合在一起，它的现代生命先始于电话线，随后转到计算机网络。

items.en: Linea meant a thread of flax and then any straight cord, and it is the source of the English noun line.
items.cn: linea 原指一根亚麻线，后来泛指任何笔直的绳索，是英语名词 line 的来源。

items.en: Old English borrowed line for a rope or a cord, and the word later also meant a row and a boundary.
items.cn: 古英语借入 line 表示绳索，这个词后来又指一排、一行以及一条界线。

items.en: In the nineteenth century a line was the wire joining two telephones, and being on the line meant being connected.
items.cn: 十九世纪，line 指连接两台电话的导线，「在线上」就意味着接通。

items.en: With computer networks the line became a data connection, and online was formed for equipment attached to it.
items.cn: 到了计算机网络时期，这条线变成数据连接，online 随之造出，用来形容接入其中的设备。

items.en: Modern English extends online from the connected device to the activity performed through it and to the content kept there.
items.cn: 现代英语把 online 从「接通的设备」扩展到「经由它完成的活动」与「存放在其中的内容」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the opposite form and other compounds built on line; the near-meaning group gathers words about networks and electronic access.
note.cn: 形近组收它的反义形式以及同样以 line 构成的复合词；近义组收表示网络与电子访问的词。

entries.definition: Not connected to a network, built with off- in place of on-.
entries.definitionCN: 不接入网络的，用 off- 替换 on- 构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: The noun at the centre of the compound, meaning a cord, a row or a connection.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词中心的名词，意为绳索、一排或一条连接。

entries.definition: Placed within a line of text, a different compound with the same second element.
entries.definitionCN: 排在文本行内的，第二个成分相同，但整体是另一个复合词。

entries.definition: The outer edge of a shape or a short summary; it shares line but not the meaning of connection.
entries.definitionCN: 形状的外缘或简要提纲；同含 line，但不表示连接。

entries.definition: Joined to a network or to another device.
entries.definitionCN: 接入网络或与另一设备相连的。

entries.definition: Stored or carried as electronic data rather than on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 以电子数据而非纸质方式存储或传输的。

entries.definition: Existing on computers or networks rather than in a physical place.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于计算机或网络中而不是实体场所的。

entries.definition: Accessed from a distance, usually through a network.
entries.definitionCN: 从远处访问的，通常经由网络。

normalIntro.en: The word pictures a machine attached to a line, and its family keeps the same thin thread running between a room and the world outside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘一台接在一条线上的机器，同族用法始终保留那根从房间伸向外界的细线。

normal.en: Line came from Latin linea, a thread, so online inherits the picture of a cord.
normal.cn: line 来自拉丁语 linea（线），所以 online 继承了「一根绳线」的画面。

normal.en: On adds the idea of being attached to or supported by that cord.
normal.cn: on 加上「附着于、由它支撑」的意思。

normal.en: Offline replaces on with off and marks a machine that has stepped away from the network.
normal.cn: offline 用 off 替换 on，标出已经离开网络的机器。

normal.en: Telephone lines gave the word its first everyday use, long before computers arrived.
normal.cn: 电话线给了这个词最早的日常用法，远在计算机出现之前。

normal.en: Online course and online shopping show the same word spreading to study and to trade.
normal.cn: online course 与 online shopping 说明同一个词又扩展到了学习与买卖。

abstract.en: Picture a single cable running out of a lit room into the dark: whatever waits at the other end becomes present on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从亮着灯的屋子伸进黑暗：另一头的一切都会出现在屏幕上。

abstract.en: Being online means the walls of the room no longer decide what you can reach.
abstract.cn: 「在线」意味着房间的墙不再决定你能触及什么。

abstract.en: The same word covers the wire, the act and the content, because a connection quietly turns into a place.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了线路、动作与内容，因为一条连接会悄悄变成一个场所。

examples.en: She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
examples.cn: 她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。

examples.en: The printer is online, so the file went straight to paper.
examples.cn: 打印机已联网，文件直接就印到了纸上。

examples.en: Most of the course materials are now online.
examples.cn: 大部分课程材料现在都在网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，来网」——哦，网来了，人就上线了；online 意为在线的、上网的。

root: 由介词 on 与名词 line 复合而成；line 源自拉丁语 linea（线、绳），十九世纪指电话线，二十世纪后期转指数据连接，于是 online 表示接入网络。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a machine attached to a line; the senses move from the connected device to the action performed through it and to the material kept there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「接在一条线上的设备」；义项从设备本身，转到经由它完成的活动，再到存放在线上的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin cable running out of a lit room into the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细线从亮着灯的屋子伸进黑暗里。

branches.en: a printer whose small light turns green
branches.cn: 打印机上的小灯转绿

branches.en: a ticket bought from a sofa late at night
branches.cn: 深夜里在沙发上买下的一张票

branches.en: a journal archive carried into the network
branches.cn: 被搬进网络的一整批过刊

branches.en: the wire and the purchase it makes possible
branches.cn: 那根线，以及它促成的这次购买

branches.en: the act of reaching a page and the page itself
branches.cn: 伸手触及一个页面的动作与页面本身

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun for a thread, the English noun built from it, and the preposition that marks attachment.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示线绳的拉丁名词、由它而来的英语名词，以及表示附着的介词支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 用于构成与线有关的复合词

items.meaning: placed within a line of text

definition_zh: 选择；选择权；被选中者；上等的；精选的
definition_en: the act of choosing between two or more things; the range offered; the thing chosen; of high quality
core_image: 面前摆着几扇门，你只能推开一扇
scene: 食堂窗口前，妈妈让我在两个套餐之间做决定。 Lunch gave me a hard choice today.
sceneCN: 这里 choice 是「选择」（第 1 个义项：在多个选项之间挑选的行为）；句意是今天午餐让我面临艰难的选择。

derivatives.zh: choice 的动词基础词，义为「挑选；决定」
由 choose 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「挑剔的；爱挑剔的」
由 choice 加后缀 -less 构成，义为「没有选择余地的」

senses.title: The act of choosing
senses.definition: the act of picking one from two or more possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 在两个以上可能性中挑出一个的行为
senses.example: It was a hard choice between art and music.
senses.exampleCN: 在美术和音乐之间做选择真难。
senses.why: The core sense names the mental act itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心义项命名了这个心理动作本身。

senses.title: The range you can choose from
senses.definition: the number or variety of things available to choose
senses.definitionCN: 可供挑选的事物的数量与种类
senses.example: The shop offers a wide choice of pens.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店的钢笔种类丰富。
senses.why: When many things lie before you, the whole spread is called a choice.
senses.whyCN: 眼前可挑的东西多了，这一整片「可选范围」也被称为 choice。

senses.title: The person or thing chosen
senses.definition: the person or thing that is picked out
senses.definitionCN: 被挑选出来的人或物
senses.example: Li Hua was our choice for team leader.
senses.exampleCN: 李华是我们选定的队长。
senses.why: The act leaves behind a result, and the result borrows the same name.
senses.whyCN: 挑选动作会留下结果，结果便沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: Of high quality; carefully picked
senses.definition: of very good quality, carefully selected
senses.definitionCN: 品质优良、经过精心挑选的
senses.example: She served us choice fruit from her garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她端出园子里精选的水果招待我们。
senses.why: Whatever survives careful choosing must be excellent.
senses.whyCN: 经过精心挑选留下来的东西必然出色，义项由此而生。

intro.en: Choice came through Old French from a Latin root about causes and deciding.
intro.cn: choice 经古法语传入，词根与拉丁语「缘由、决定」相关。

items.en: Latin causa meant cause or reason, and causari meant to plead a case.
items.cn: 拉丁语 causa 指缘由，causari 指为案件辩护。

items.en: Old French choisir grew out of this, meaning to choose or to weigh reasons.
items.cn: 古法语 choisir 由此发展而来，义为「挑选；权衡缘由」。

items.en: Old French chois was the noun form, the act or result of choosing.
items.cn: 古法语名词 chois 即「挑选」这一行为或结果。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it as chois around the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 十三世纪前后，中古英语借入为 chois。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling as choice and added the adjective sense.
items.cn: 现代英语定型拼写为 choice，并发展出形容词义。

note.en: The first group shows the choose family; the second gathers words about picking.
note.cn: 第一组展示 choose 词族，第二组收与挑选相关的词。

entries.definition: A group of singers in a church or school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合唱团」，拼写与 choice 相近但读音不同。

entries.definition: The ringing sound of a bell.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钟声；编钟」，词形与 choice 相近。

entries.definition: The sound made when speaking or singing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「嗓音」，词尾与 choice 同为 -oice 音。

entries.definition: One thing that can be chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选项」，指可选的单一项目。

entries.definition: The act or result of choosing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挑选；选集」，较正式。

entries.definition: One of two or more possible choices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「替代选项」，强调另一条路。

normalIntro.en: Remember choice as the noun partner of choose.
normalIntro.cn: 把 choice 记成 choose 的名词搭档。

normal.en: choose is the verb; choice is its noun.
normal.cn: choose 是动词，choice 是它的名词。

normal.en: make a choice is the fixed verb phrase.
normal.cn: make a choice 是固定搭配。

normal.en: have no choice means you must do it.
normal.cn: have no choice 表示别无选择。

normal.en: plural spelling changes y to i: choices.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 i，写作 choices。

normal.en: first choice means the option you prefer most.
normal.cn: first choice 指最中意的选项。

abstract.en: See several doors, of which only one may open.
abstract.cn: 想象几扇门，其中只有一扇可以推开。

abstract.en: Feel the pause between two paths before stepping out.
abstract.cn: 感受踏出脚步前在两条路之间的停顿。

abstract.en: Hear the quiet click of a decision being made.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见决定落下时轻轻的一声脆响。

examples.en: You must make a choice before Friday.
examples.cn: 你必须在周五之前做出选择。

examples.en: There were many choices on the menu.
examples.cn: 菜单上的选择很多。

examples.en: She had no choice but to wait.
examples.cn: 她别无选择，只能等待。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巧伊斯」——巧的是伊斯手气好，抽中了心仪的选择。

root: 拉丁语 causa（缘由）→ 古法语 choisir（挑选）、chois（名词）→ 中古英语 chois → 现代英语 choice；同族词有 choose（动词）、choosy（挑剔的）。

sensesIntro.en: Choice moves from the act of picking to the options, the result and top quality.
sensesIntro.cn: choice 从挑选行为延伸到选项范围、被选结果和上等品质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing before options and picking one
core.cn: 核心意象：面对选项挑出一个

branches.en: The act of choosing
branches.cn: 挑选这一行为

branches.en: The range on offer
branches.cn: 可供挑选的范围

branches.en: The one that gets picked
branches.cn: 最终被选中的人或物

branches.en: Carefully selected quality
branches.cn: 精选出的上等品质

branches.en: The freedom to decide
branches.cn: 决定的权利

intro.en: Choice carries the old French ending -ise from the verb choisir.
intro.cn: choice 保留了古法语动词 choisir 的结尾。

latinIntro.en: The deep root is Latin causa, shared with words about reasons.
latinIntro.cn: 更深的词根是拉丁语 causa，与表示「缘由」的词同源。

items.example: The cause of the fire is unclear.

items.meaning: the act or result of choosing

items.example: Bus is the alternative to walking.
items.exampleCN: 坐公交是不步行的另一选择。

items.example: She has a preference for tea.

definition_zh: 贫穷的；穷困的；差的；低劣的；可怜的；贫瘠的；缺乏……的
definition_en: having very little money, of low quality, deserving pity, or lacking something that is needed
core_image: 一件短了一截的旧外套，袖口磨得发白，衣袋里空空如也
scene: 冬天的清晨，屋里没有暖气，孩子的外套短了一截，袖口磨得发白。 The family was too poor to buy coal that winter.
sceneCN: 这里的 poor 是「贫穷的」（第 1 个义项：缺钱）；句意为那个冬天这家人穷得买不起煤。图中可辨识物件：短了一截的外套、磨白的袖口、没有暖气的屋子。

pos.zh: 贫穷的；穷困的；差的；低劣的；可怜的；贫瘠的；缺乏……的

derivatives.zh: 由 poor 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「很差地；不力地」；作形容词时指「身体不适的」
与 poor 同出拉丁语 pauper，经古法语 poverte 而来，义为「贫困；匮乏」
由 poor 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「贫穷；低劣」

senses.title: Having very little money
senses.definition: having so little money that ordinary needs such as food, heat or clothing are hard to meet
senses.definitionCN: 钱少到难以应付吃饭、取暖、穿衣这类日常需要
senses.example: The family was too poor to heat the house.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人穷得连房子都供不起暖气。
senses.why: Latin pauper described a person of small means, and the word came into English through French carrying that plain material sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pauper 形容家底微薄的人，这个词经法语进入英语时，带的就是这层朴素的物质含义。

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: not as good as it should be in strength, sound, finish or standard
senses.definitionCN: 在结实、清晰、做工或水准上达不到应有的程度
senses.example: The recording was poor and hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 录音效果很差，听不太清楚。
senses.why: A person can be poor in money, so a thing can be poor in what it ought to have; the same measure of lack is applied to quality.
senses.whyCN: 人可以穷在钱上，东西也可以穷在它本该有的地方；判断质量用的仍是同一把「缺」的尺子。

senses.title: Deserving pity
senses.definition: unfortunate enough to make other people feel sorry for them
senses.definitionCN: 处境不幸，使别人替其难过
senses.example: The poor dog waited in the rain for its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 那只可怜的狗在雨里等着主人。
senses.why: Someone who has too little is exposed to harm, so the word slides from naming the lack to naming the feeling that lack stirs in others.
senses.whyCN: 拥有的太少就容易受伤害，于是这个词从指「缺」滑向指「缺」在旁人心里激起的怜惜。

senses.title: Lacking a needed substance
senses.definition: containing too little of something that plants or bodies need, as in poor soil or water poor in minerals
senses.definitionCN: 所含的植物或身体所需之物太少，如贫瘠的土壤、缺少矿物质的水
senses.example: This soil is too poor for wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 这土太贫瘠，种不了小麦。
senses.why: The oldest frame survives in phrases such as poor in iron, where the word simply marks what a thing does not have enough of.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的结构留在 poor in iron 这类说法里，那里的 poor 只是标出一件东西哪一样不够。

intro.en: Poor comes from Latin pauper through Old French, and the whole family keeps the idea of having or producing too little.
intro.cn: poor 经古法语来自拉丁语 pauper，整族词都保留着「拥有或产出太少」的意思。

items.en: Pauper meant poor or of small means, and it could even describe soil that yields little.
items.cn: pauper 意为贫穷的、家底薄的，甚至能形容产出很少的土地。

items.en: The noun paupertas named poverty and want, and it is the source of the English word poverty.
items.cn: 名词 paupertas 指贫困与匮乏，是英语 poverty 的来源。

items.en: Old French povre kept both the material sense and a stronger tone of wretchedness and misfortune.
items.cn: 古法语的 povre 既保留物质上的贫穷，也带有更重的凄惨与不幸意味。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as povre and poure competed, and the form with -ou- became the standard poor.
items.cn: 中古英语的 povre、poure 等拼写并行，带 -ou- 的形式最终成为标准拼写 poor。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from money to quality, health, soil and finally to a tone of pity.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从钱财扩展到质量、健康、土壤，最后还带上了一层怜悯的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin stem or the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for having little, being bad or deserving pity.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁词干或读音相近的词；近义组收表示「贫穷」「差」「可怜」的词。

entries.definition: A very poor person, especially one supported by charity.
entries.definitionCN: 穷人；靠救济生活的人。

entries.definition: The state of being poor; a lack of something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困；匮乏。

entries.definition: A tiny opening in skin or in a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 毛孔；气孔。

entries.definition: Having very little money and needing help.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困的；需要帮助的。

entries.definition: Having no money at all.
entries.definitionCN: 身无分文的。

entries.definition: Of low quality or below an acceptable standard.
entries.definitionCN: 坏的；差的；不合标准的。

entries.definition: Arousing sympathy because of suffering or weakness.
entries.definitionCN: 令人同情的；可怜的。

normalIntro.en: Poor is a Latin word for small means, and its family shows how a judgement about money becomes a judgement about quality and then a feeling of pity.
normalIntro.cn: poor 是拉丁语中表示「家底薄」的词，它这一族显示了关于钱的判断如何变成关于质量的判断，再变成怜悯。

normal.en: Pauper is the Latin word itself used as an English noun: a pauper is a person who is poor.
normal.cn: pauper 就是那个拉丁词直接当英语名词用：a pauper 就是穷人。

normal.en: Poverty comes from Latin paupertas, the noun built beside pauper, so the two words are cousins rather than parent and child.
normal.cn: poverty 来自拉丁语 paupertas，是与 pauper 并列造出的名词，所以两者是表亲，而不是父子。

normal.en: Old French povre lost its ending on the way into English, leaving the short form poor.
normal.cn: 古法语的 povre 在进入英语的路上丢掉了词尾，留下短短的 poor。

normal.en: Poor quality and poor health both keep the original idea of lacking what should be there.
normal.cn: poor quality 与 poor health 都保留了原来的意思：缺了本该有的东西。

normal.en: The poor is an adjective standing in for a noun, so it takes a plural verb: the poor are, not the poor is.
normal.cn: the poor 是形容词顶替名词，所以配复数动词：说 the poor are，不说 the poor is。

abstract.en: A word for having too little turns into a word for being bad, which shows how easily a judgement about means becomes a judgement about worth.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有太少」的词变成了表示「不好」的词，说明对家底的判断多容易变成对价值的判断。

abstract.en: Calling a dog poor does not measure its money; it measures the gap between what it has and what it needs.
abstract.cn: 把一只狗叫作 poor，量的不是它的钱，而是它拥有的与它需要的之间的差距。

abstract.en: Poor soil and a poor excuse share one grammar: something is missing that the situation requires.
abstract.cn: 贫瘠的土壤与蹩脚的借口共用一个语法：这情形需要的东西缺了。

examples.en: The family was too poor to heat the house.
examples.cn: 这家人穷得连房子都供不起暖气。

examples.en: The recording was poor and hard to follow.
examples.cn: 录音效果很差，听不太清楚。

examples.en: This soil is too poor for wheat.
examples.cn: 这土太贫瘠，种不了小麦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破」——穷得衣服都破了；记住 poor 是贫穷的。

root: 经古法语 povre 来自拉丁语 pauper（贫穷的、少产的）；pauper 的更早来源不确定，一般认为与「产出少」有关。同族词有 poverty、pauper。

sensesIntro.en: The core is having too little; the branches apply that lack to money, to quality, to the feeling of pity, and to soil or water short of a substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拥有的太少」；各分支把这种「缺」分别用到钱财、质量、怜悯之情，以及缺某种成分的土壤或水。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty pocket and a coat whose sleeves have worn thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：空空的口袋，和袖口磨得又薄又短的外套。

branches.en: a cold room where the heating has been switched off
branches.cn: 暖气关掉的冷屋子

branches.en: a crackling recording that swallows the speaker's words
branches.cn: 吞掉说话人字句的沙沙录音

branches.en: a wet dog waiting by a gate for its owner
branches.cn: 在门口雨里等主人的湿狗

branches.en: a field where wheat will not grow
branches.cn: 长不出小麦的一块地

branches.en: the same shortfall, judged once as quality and once as misfortune
branches.cn: 同一种「缺」，一次被判为质量差，一次被判为不幸

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin adjective of small means, its noun and verb, and two English suffixes that make an adverb and a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示家底薄的拉丁形容词及其名词、动词承载，再加上两个英语后缀，构成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 倒；灌；倾泻；大量涌入；倾诉；浇筑
definition_en: to make a liquid flow out of a container, to cause people or things to move in a steady stream, to rain very heavily, to tell feelings freely, or to cast wet concrete
core_image: 一只手把壶嘴压低，水柱落进杯里，杯口腾起一点热气
scene: 屋檐下的水线连成一片，院里的人抱着盆往外泼。 It had poured all night, and the lane was ankle-deep in water.
sceneCN: 这里 pour 指「大雨倾盆而下」（第 3 个义项：雨下得又急又密）；句意为雨下了一整夜，巷子里的水已经没到脚踝。图中可辨识场景：连成水线的屋檐、往外泼水的盆、漫过路面的积水。

pos.zh: 倒；灌；倾泻；涌入；倾诉；浇筑

derivatives.zh: 由 down 与 pour 复合而成，义为「倾盆大雨」
由 out 与 pouring 复合而成，义为「倾泻；情感的流露」
由 pour 加表示人或物的 -er 构成，义为「倒液体的人或器具」

senses.title: To make a liquid flow from a container
senses.definition: to hold a container at an angle so that the liquid inside runs out into another vessel
senses.definitionCN: 把容器倾斜，让里面的液体流进另一个器皿
senses.example: She poured the tea slowly so that the leaves stayed in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢地倒茶，让茶叶留在壶里。
senses.why: The oldest recorded use is simply liquid leaving a vessel, and every later sense keeps that picture of something flowing out under control.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早用法就是液体离开容器，后来每个义项都保留着这幅画面：有东西在控制之下流出来。

senses.title: To move in a continuous stream
senses.definition: to come or go somewhere in large numbers and without a break, like a liquid that will not stop
senses.definitionCN: 像止不住的液体一样，大批而不间断地来或去
senses.example: Fans poured out of the stadium as the final whistle blew.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响，球迷从体育场里涌了出来。
senses.why: A crowd moves like a liquid when it is dense enough, so English uses the same verb for people, letters and money arriving in an unbroken flow.
senses.whyCN: 人群一旦密集，移动起来就像液体，于是英语用同一个动词来说人、信件和钱源源不断地到来。

senses.title: To rain very heavily
senses.definition: to rain hard and steadily, so that water seems to be tipped out of the sky
senses.definitionCN: 雨下得又急又密，仿佛天上有水被整盆倒下
senses.example: It poured all afternoon, and nobody left the house.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午都在下倾盆大雨，谁也没出门。
senses.why: Rain is water falling in sheets, so the verb of tipping out a vessel transfers to the sky itself, especially in the impersonal phrase it is pouring.
senses.whyCN: 雨就是成片落下的水，于是「把容器倒空」的动词被挪到天上，尤其在 it is pouring 这种无人称说法里。

senses.title: To tell feelings without holding back
senses.definition: to express feelings or a story freely and at length, as if emptying what is inside
senses.definitionCN: 把心里的感受或经历毫无保留地、连续地说出来
senses.example: She poured out the whole story to a friend at the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在厨房桌边，把整件事都向朋友倾诉了出来。
senses.why: If a vessel can be emptied, so can a person, and pour out turns the chest into a container whose contents finally leave.
senses.whyCN: 容器能被倒空，人也可以；pour out 把胸腔变成一只容器，里面的东西终于流了出来。

senses.title: To cast wet concrete or metal
senses.definition: to fill a mould or a prepared space with wet concrete or molten metal so that it sets into shape
senses.definitionCN: 把湿混凝土或熔化的金属灌进模子或备好的空间，让它凝固成形
senses.example: The crew poured the foundation before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在下雨之前浇好了地基。
senses.why: Building work borrows the kitchen verb because wet concrete is a heavy liquid that has to be tipped into a prepared shape and left to harden.
senses.whyCN: 建筑行当借用这个厨房动词，因为湿混凝土就是一种沉重的液体，要倒进备好的形状里，再等它变硬。

intro.en: Pour is a Middle English verb whose origin is uncertain. The usual guess points to Old French, but no link has been proved, and the word has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: pour 是中古英语的一个动词，来源不确定。常见的猜测指向古法语，但没有得到证实，这个词也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: Pour first appears around the fourteenth century as pouren, meaning to flow, gush or tip liquid out; the earlier history is not recorded.
items.cn: pour 约在十四世纪以 pouren 的形式出现，意为流出、涌出、把液体倒出；更早的来历没有记录。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a link with Old French purer, to pour out or strain, but the connection remains a guess rather than an established borrowing.
items.cn: 有些词典猜测它与古法语 purer（倒出、滤出）有关，但这只是一种猜测，并未确立为借词关系。

items.en: The verb widened from liquid in a cup to crowds leaving a gate and to rain falling in sheets, because all three move in one unbroken flow.
items.cn: 这个动词从杯里的液体扩展到涌出大门的人群与成片落下的雨，因为三者都是不间断地流动。

items.en: With modern building work the verb took on concrete and metal, which are liquids only until they set.
items.cn: 随着近代建筑工程，这个动词用到了混凝土与金属上，而它们只在凝固之前是液体。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense and adds the emotional one, so a person may pour tea, pour out a story, or stand in the pouring rain.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物理义，又添了情感义，所以一个人可以倒茶、倾诉一件事，也可以站在倾盆大雨里。

note.en: The look-alike group puts two spellings that merely sound the same beside the word's own derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for liquid on the move.
note.cn: 形近组把两个只是读音相同的拼写与本词自己的派生词放在一起；近义组收表示液体流动的动词。

entries.definition: A tiny opening in skin or in a leaf; also to study a text closely.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤或叶片上的小孔；也指细读；这只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having little money or little quality.
entries.definitionCN: 缺钱的；质量差的；这只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person or vessel that pours liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 倒液体的人或器具。

entries.definition: A sudden heavy fall of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 突如其来的倾盆大雨。

entries.definition: To let liquid fall out of a container by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 不慎让液体从容器里洒出。

entries.definition: To move steadily and smoothly, as a liquid does.
entries.definitionCN: 像液体一样平稳不断地移动。

entries.definition: To move in a continuous current.
entries.definitionCN: 以连续的水流般移动。

entries.definition: To flow out suddenly and in large amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 突然大量涌出。

normalIntro.en: There is no Latin root to lean on here, so the word is best held by its pictures: a tipped jug, a crowd at a gate, a sky emptied out.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词根可依靠，最好用画面来记住它：倾斜的壶、门口的人群、被倒空的天。

normal.en: Pour out and pour into are the two directions: out of a container, into another place or crowd.
normal.cn: pour out 与 pour into 是两个方向：从容器里出来，进入另一个地方或人群。

normal.en: Downpour adds down to pour, and English rain does fall down, so the compound needs no explanation.
normal.cn: downpour 在 pour 前加 down，英语的雨本来就是往下落的，所以这个复合词不必多解释。

normal.en: Outpouring keeps the same movement for feelings: what was inside comes out in quantity.
normal.cn: outpouring 把同一种流动用在情感上：原本在里面的东西大量地出来了。

normal.en: Pourer adds -er, so the word can name a person or a jug designed to pour cleanly.
normal.cn: pourer 加 -er，于是这个词既能指人，也能指专门设计来倒得干净的壶。

normal.en: It is pouring is impersonal, like it is raining: the sky, not a person, is doing the pouring.
normal.cn: it is pouring 是无人称句，和 it is raining 一样：倒水的是天，不是人。

abstract.en: Pour is what happens when a boundary is opened: a jug, a gate, a heart, a mould.
abstract.cn: pour 说的是边界被打开的那一刻：壶口、门口、心口、模子口。

abstract.en: The same verb covers tea and rain because both are water that has stopped being held.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词能管茶也能管雨，因为两者都是不再被兜住的水。

abstract.en: To pour out a story is to treat words as something liquid and finite, stored until it runs.
abstract.cn: 把故事倾诉出来，就是把话语当成一种有限的水，一直存着，直到流尽。

examples.en: She poured the tea slowly into four cups.
examples.cn: 她把茶慢慢倒进四只杯子里。

examples.en: It poured all night and the lane flooded.
examples.cn: 雨下了一整夜，巷子都淹了。

examples.en: He poured out his worries to an old friend.
examples.cn: 他把心里的烦恼向一位老朋友倾诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼」——泼水出去就是 pour；雨大得整盆往下倒，也说 it is pouring。

root: 中古英语 pouren（涌出、倾倒），约十四世纪见于记录，更早来源不确定；有词典猜测与古法语 purer（倒出、滤出）有关，但未成定论，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all describe something leaving a boundary in a steady flow: liquid, a crowd, rain, feeling, wet concrete.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项说的都是某种东西越过边界、连续流出：液体、人群、雨、情感、湿混凝土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tipping a jug lower, a thin column of water dropping into a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把壶压得更低，一条细水柱落进杯里。

branches.en: a teapot tilted until the last drop leaves
branches.cn: 茶壶被倾到最后一滴流出

branches.en: a gate opening onto a river of people
branches.cn: 大门打开，人群像河水涌出

branches.en: a gutter overflowing while the sky stays grey
branches.cn: 天还灰着，排水沟已经溢出

branches.en: words coming faster than the listener can nod
branches.cn: 话说得比听的人点头还快

branches.en: wet concrete sliding down a wooden form
branches.cn: 湿混凝土顺着木模滑下

intro.en: With no Latin stem behind it, the word is held together by English pieces: the base verb, its participles, -er for the vessel, and the compounds down and out.
intro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词干，靠英语自身的部件撑起来：基础动词、它的分词、表示器具的 -er，以及 down 与 out 两个复合成分。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
