definition_zh: 打；敲；击败；搅打；节拍；跳动
definition_en: to hit something again and again, or to win against someone
core_image: 鼓槌一下一下落下，鼓面震出连续的声响
scene: 决赛最后一分钟，我们队又进一球，赢了对手。 Our team beat the other class in the final match.
sceneCN: 这里 beat 是「击败」（第 2 个义项：在比赛或竞争中胜过对方）；句意为我们队在决赛中战胜了另一个班。

derivatives.zh: 由 beat 加 -ing 构成，义为「敲打；跳动」
由 beat 的过去分词转化而来，义为「被打败的；被敲打的」
由否定前缀 un- 与 beaten 构成，义为「未被击败的」
由 beat 加 -er 构成，义为「搅拌器；敲打者」

senses.title: To hit again and again
senses.definition: to hit something many times with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力反复击打某物
senses.example: He beat the drum during the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 游行时他敲着鼓。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to strike, so repeated striking is the oldest and most physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义就是「击打」，所以反复击打是最古老、最具体的义项。

senses.title: To defeat
senses.definition: to win against someone in a game, fight, or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、打斗或竞争中胜过对方
senses.example: Our team beat the other class in the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队在决赛中战胜了另一个班。
senses.why: A fight is a series of blows, and the one still standing has beaten the other, so striking grows into defeating.
senses.whyCN: 打斗是一连串的击打，还站着的一方就「打」赢了对方，于是「击打」长成了「击败」。

senses.title: To mix food quickly
senses.definition: to mix eggs, cream, or batter quickly with a fork or machine
senses.definitionCN: 用叉子或机器快速搅拌鸡蛋、奶油或面糊
senses.example: Beat the eggs before you add the milk.
senses.exampleCN: 加牛奶之前先把鸡蛋打散。
senses.why: Rapid stirring is a kind of repeated striking against the mixture, so the same verb serves the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 快速搅拌就是对混合物反复击打，所以同一个动词也进了厨房。

senses.title: A regular rhythm
senses.definition: the regular strong pulse in music or in a poem
senses.definitionCN: 音乐或诗歌中规律出现的强拍
senses.example: The drummer kept a steady beat for the whole song.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手整首歌都保持着稳定的节拍。
senses.why: A drum is struck again and again at equal intervals, and the pattern of strikes becomes the beat.
senses.whyCN: 鼓被等间隔地反复敲击，这些敲击形成的规律就成了「节拍」。

senses.title: To pulse
senses.definition: to move or sound with a regular pulse, as the heart does
senses.definitionCN: 像心脏那样规律地跳动或发出声响
senses.example: Her heart beat fast after the race.
senses.exampleCN: 赛跑之后她的心跳得很快。
senses.why: The heart strikes the chest from inside with a regular rhythm, so the verb moves from drum to body.
senses.whyCN: 心脏在胸腔里规律地撞击，于是这个动词从鼓面移到了身体上。

intro.en: Beat is a native English verb with a Germanic root and a strong, irregular past form.
intro.cn: beat 是本族英语动词，源于日耳曼语，过去式与过去分词为不规则的强变化形式。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to strike lies behind the Germanic verb.
items.cn: 一个可重构、意为「击打」的词根，是这一日耳曼语动词的远源。

items.en: The Germanic verb bautan meant to beat or to strike.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词 bautan 意为「打、击」。

items.en: Old English beatan meant to strike repeatedly, and it kept a strong past participle.
items.cn: 古英语 beatan 意为「反复击打」，并保留了强变化的过去分词。

items.en: The sense of defeating an opponent grows from the image of a fight.
items.cn: 「击败对手」的义项从打斗的意象中发展出来。

items.en: Music and the heart give the noun its sense of a regular pulse.
items.cn: 音乐与心脏赋予名词「规律搏动」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and derivatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for striking and winning.
note.cn: 形近组收这个动词的形式与派生词；近义组收表示击打与获胜的其他动词。

entries.definition: The past participle, also used as an adjective meaning defeated or worn by blows.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，也作形容词，义为「被打败的、被敲打的」。

entries.definition: The act of striking, or a regular pulsing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敲打；搏动」，由 beat 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A tool or person that beats, such as an egg beater.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「搅拌器；敲打者」，如打蛋器。

entries.definition: A root vegetable; it sounds the same but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甜菜」；读音相同，但词源来自另一个拉丁词，与 beat 无关。

entries.definition: To strike once; it does not suggest repetition like beat.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打、击中」，通常指一次，而不像 beat 强调反复。

entries.definition: To hit with force, often once and deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击、打」，常指一次有意的重击。

entries.definition: To win against someone; the formal word for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击败」，是第二个义项的正式说法。

entries.definition: A regular pattern of sounds; it is close to the noun sense of beat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节奏」，与 beat 的名词义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real strong forms beat and beaten, the suffixes, and the fixed phrases with beat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的强变化形式 beat 与 beaten、后缀，以及 beat 的固定搭配。

normal.en: The past tense is beat and the past participle is beaten, so the verb keeps an old strong pattern.
normal.cn: 过去式是 beat，过去分词是 beaten，这个动词保留了古老的强变化模式。

normal.en: Beat the drum is the literal action that gave the word its musical sense.
normal.cn: beat the drum 正是赋予这个词音乐义的字面动作。

normal.en: Beat eggs means stir them hard, as if striking them again and again.
normal.cn: beat eggs 意为用力搅打，好像反复击打它们。

normal.en: Unbeaten means no one has ever beaten that team.
normal.cn: unbeaten 意为从未有队伍击败过它。

normal.en: Beat about the bush means going around the point instead of hitting it directly.
normal.cn: beat about the bush 意为绕着话题走，而不直接点中要害。

abstract.en: Picture a drum skin: each blow fades fast, but the next one comes at the same distance, and that spacing is rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象一张鼓面：每一下很快消失，但下一下总在同样的间隔到来，这个间隔就是节奏。

abstract.en: A fight and a football match share one verb, because both end when one side can no longer answer.
abstract.cn: 打斗与足球赛共用一个动词，因为两者都在一方无法回应时结束。

abstract.en: The heart does the drummer's work without a drummer, which is why the same word covers music and pulse.
abstract.cn: 心脏在没有鼓手的情况下做着鼓手的事，所以同一个词既指音乐也指脉搏。

examples.en: Our team beat the other class in the final match.
examples.cn: 我们队在决赛中战胜了另一个班。

examples.en: He beat the drum during the parade.
examples.cn: 游行时他敲着鼓。

examples.en: Her heart beat fast after the race.
examples.cn: 赛跑之后她的心跳得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必特」——鼓点必特别准，一下一下打在节拍上：敲打、节拍

root: beat 来自古英语 beatan「反复击打」，源于日耳曼语 bautan，可上溯到原始印欧语中意为「击打」的重构词根。由「击打」引申出「击败」「搅打」，又由鼓的反复敲击引申出名词「节拍」与「心跳」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of beat all come from repeated striking: hitting, defeating, stirring food, the pattern of drum strikes, and the pulse of the heart.
sensesIntro.cn: beat 的五个义项都来自反复击打：打、击败、搅打食物、鼓点的规律，以及心脏的搏动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drumstick falls on the skin again and again at equal intervals.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓槌一下一下，以相等的间隔落在鼓面上。

branches.en: THE STRIKE: the oldest sense is plain repeated hitting.
branches.cn: 击打线：最古老的义项就是单纯反复地打。

branches.en: THE FIGHT: the side that keeps striking wins, so hitting becomes defeating.
branches.cn: 胜负线：还能继续打的一方获胜，于是「打」变成「击败」。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN: fast stirring is striking the mixture again and again.
branches.cn: 厨房线：快速搅拌就是反复击打混合物。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: equal spacing between drum strikes becomes musical beat.
branches.cn: 规律线：鼓击之间相等的间隔成了音乐的节拍。

branches.en: THE BODY: the heart repeats the drummer's action inside the chest.
branches.cn: 身体线：心脏在胸腔里重复着鼓手的动作。

intro.en: Beat is a strong Germanic verb, so it marks tense by changing its vowel rather than adding -ed.
intro.cn: beat 是日耳曼语强变化动词，靠改变元音而非加 -ed 来表示时态。

latinIntro.en: Latin battuere also meant to beat, but it is a separate root and not a cognate, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 battuere 也意为「打」，但那是另一个词根，并非同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: He beat the door with his fist.

items.meaning: a person or tool that does

items.exampleCN: 它与 beat 构成 beat up。
它与 beat 构成 beat down。

definition_zh: 迅速的；急剧的；急流
definition_en: moving or happening very quickly; happening suddenly and to a great degree; a part of a river where the water flows fast and rough over rocks
core_image: 河水在乱石间奔涌成一道白色的急流
scene: 山谷里的河水撞上乱石，翻起白色的浪头，一路奔涌而下。 The river's rapid current swept the boat downstream in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 rapid 是「迅速的」（第 1 个义项：移动或发生得极快）；句意为河中湍急的水流几秒钟就把小船冲向下游。画面里可留意：翻白的浪头、乱石、被冲走的小船。

derivatives.zh: rapid 加 -ly，指迅速地
rapid 加 -ity，指迅速、快捷
rapid 加 -s，指河中湍急的一段
rapid 加 -ness，指迅速的状态

senses.title: Moving very quickly
senses.definition: moving or happening at great speed
senses.definitionCN: 以极快的速度移动或发生
senses.example: The country has seen rapid economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家经历了迅速的经济增长。
senses.why: Latin rapidus described anything carried along swiftly, and the word kept that plain sense of speed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rapidus 形容任何被迅速带走之物，这个词保留了这层朴素的「快」。

senses.title: Sudden and great in degree
senses.definition: happening suddenly and to a large degree, used especially of change
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生且幅度很大，尤用于变化
senses.example: A rapid change in the weather caught the climbers off guard.
senses.exampleCN: 天气的急剧变化让登山者措手不及。
senses.why: Something carried away fast can also change fast, so rapid extended from speed of motion to speed of change.
senses.whyCN: 被迅速带走之物也会迅速改变，于是 rapid 从运动之快扩展到变化之快。

senses.title: Fast rough water
senses.definition: a stretch of river where the water runs fast and breaks over rocks
senses.definitionCN: 河水中流得很快、在岩石上翻涌的一段
senses.example: The raft bounced through the rapids.
senses.exampleCN: 木筏在急流中颠簸而过。
senses.why: The same image of water seized and carried along named the place in a river where the current runs hardest.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「水被卷走」的意象，命名了河中水流最猛的那一段。

intro.en: Rapid goes back to Latin rapere, to seize and carry away; what is rapid is literally carried along at speed.
intro.cn: rapid 可追溯到拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走）；被 rapid 形容之物，字面上就是被迅速卷走的。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off, and it pictured force dragging something away.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走，画面是力量把某物拖走。

items.en: Rapidus described anything carried along swiftly, from a rushing river to a fast flight.
items.cn: rapidus 形容任何被迅速带走之物，从奔腾的河到飞快的飞行。

items.en: Old French took the Latin word as rapide and kept the sense of great speed.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词借作 rapide，保留了「极快」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rapid applied the word to motion, to events, and to rivers that run fast.
items.cn: 中古英语 rapid 把这个词用于运动、事件，以及流得快的河。

items.en: Modern English uses rapid for quick motion and quick change, and the plural rapids for rough, fast water.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rapid 指快速运动与快速变化，用复数 rapids 指湍急的水流。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and one word from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers ordinary words for speed.
note.cn: 形近组收同根的形式与一个同源词；近义组收表示速度的常用词。

entries.definition: At great speed.
entries.definitionCN: 以极快速度。

entries.definition: The quality of being fast.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速的性质。

entries.definition: A stretch of fast, rough river water.
entries.definitionCN: 一段湍急的河水。

entries.definition: The act of seizing property by force, from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力夺取财物，同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: Moving or happening at high speed.
entries.definitionCN: 高速移动或发生的。

entries.definition: Moving or done in a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在短时间内移动或完成的。

entries.definition: Moving very fast, often smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 移动极快，常含顺畅之意。

entries.definition: Characterized by speed.
entries.definitionCN: 以速度为特征的。

normalIntro.en: The word pictures things seized and carried along; from that force come the senses of fast motion, fast change and fast water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的画面是被抓住并卷走的东西；从这股力量生出快速运动、快速变化与湍急水流三层意思。

normal.en: Rapid and rapere share the image of something seized and carried off at speed.
normal.cn: rapid 与 rapere 共享「某物被抓住并迅速卷走」的画面。

normal.en: Rapids are the parts of a river where the water itself runs fast.
normal.cn: rapids 就是河中水本身流得最快的地方。

normal.en: Rapid growth and rapid change both describe movement in time, not in space.
normal.cn: rapid growth 与 rapid change 描述的都是时间中的移动，而不是空间中的移动。

normal.en: Rapid is stronger than quick: it suggests real force behind the speed.
normal.cn: rapid 比 quick 更强，暗含速度背后有一股真实的力量。

normal.en: The same root gives rapine, the taking of goods by force.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 rapine，即用武力夺取财物。

abstract.en: Speed that carries things away is the oldest sense of rapid.
abstract.cn: 「把东西卷走的快」是 rapid 最古老的意思。

abstract.en: We call change rapid when it moves faster than we can follow.
abstract.cn: 当变化快过我们跟上的速度，我们才称它 rapid。

abstract.en: A rapid is water in a hurry, and that is the word's whole picture.
abstract.cn: 急流是匆匆赶路的水，这就是这个词的全部画面。

examples.en: The country has seen rapid economic growth.
examples.cn: 这个国家经历了迅速的经济增长。

examples.en: A rapid change in the weather caught the climbers off guard.
examples.cn: 天气的急剧变化让登山者措手不及。

examples.en: The raft bounced through the rapids.
examples.cn: 木筏在急流中颠簸而过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拉皮的」——被人拽着飞快拖走，记住 rapid 是迅速的。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住带走）→ rapidus（被迅速带走的）→ 古法语 rapide → 现代英语 rapid；同族有 rapidly、rapidity、rapids。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being seized and carried along; the senses divide into fast motion, fast change, and fast rough water.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抓住并卷走」；义项分为快速运动、快速变化与湍急的水流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current of white water tearing through rocks and dragging everything with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股白色的水流撕开乱石，把一切都拖走。

branches.en: a sprinter leaving the blocks
branches.cn: 冲出起跑器的短跑者

branches.en: a price line climbing steeply
branches.cn: 陡直上扬的价格曲线

branches.en: white water breaking over rocks
branches.cn: 漫过岩石的白色激流

branches.en: speed in motion and speed in change
branches.cn: 运动之快与变化之快

branches.en: a fast runner and a fast river
branches.cn: 飞快的奔跑者与湍急的河流

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes and compounds on the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由同一词根上的英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the word its root: rapere, to seize, and rapidus, carried swiftly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给了这个词词根：rapere（抓住）与 rapidus（被迅速带走）。

definition_zh: 教育；培养；教育学；（尤指）学校教育体系
definition_en: the process of teaching and learning, especially in schools, and the organized system that carries it out
core_image: 午后教室里的黑板、成排课桌与摊开的课本，窗台上摆着一只装满粉笔的旧铁盒
scene: 乡村学校的教室里，黑板擦得发亮，课桌排成几行，课本摊在桌面上。 Public education gave every child in the valley a seat and a teacher.
sceneCN: 这里指「教与学的过程，尤指学校中的教育」（第 1 个义项：传授与习得知识的过程）；句意为公共教育让山谷里的每个孩子都有了座位和老师。可辨识物件：黑板、课桌、课本、粉笔盒。

pos.zh: 教育；培养；教育学（通常不可数；指一种教育经历时可加不定冠词）

forms.label: 形容词（教育的；教育性的）

derivatives.zh: 教育；培养
受过教育的
教育的；有教育意义的
教育工作者
教育学家；教育改革者
有教育作用的

senses.title: The process of teaching and learning
senses.definition: the activity through which knowledge, skills and habits are passed from one person to another
senses.definitionCN: 知识、技能与习惯在人与人之间传递的活动
senses.example: Good education begins with questions rather than answers.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教育从提问而不是从答案开始。
senses.why: the noun came from a verb meaning to bring up and rear, so its core is the whole act of raising someone's mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自表「养育、培养」的动词，其核心是把人的心智养成的整个动作。

senses.title: The school system
senses.definition: the organized network of schools, teachers, curricula and funding that a state or community maintains
senses.definitionCN: 国家或社区维持的学校、教师、课程与经费的组织网络
senses.example: Rural education improved after the new schools opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校开办之后，乡村教育得到改善。
senses.why: once schooling became a public service, the word shifted from the act to the machine that delivers it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦学校教育成为公共服务，这个词就从动作转向提供它的那台机器。

senses.title: A person's upbringing and formation
senses.titleCN: 一个人的教养与成长背景
senses.definition: the whole formation of a person's character and taste, including what happens outside school
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格与品味所受的整体养成，包括校门之外的部分
senses.example: Her education at home was stricter than anything the school imposed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在家所受的教养比学校的一切要求都更严格。
senses.why: the older sense of rearing survives in phrases about a person's background rather than a system.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「养育」义保留在谈论个人背景的短语里，而不指体系。

senses.title: The academic field of study
senses.definition: the discipline that studies how people learn and how teaching should be organized
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何学习、教学应如何组织的学科
senses.example: She holds a doctorate in education from a state university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所州立大学取得教育学博士学位。
senses.why: a field of study takes the name of its object, which is why the discipline is simply called education.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科常以其研究对象命名，因此这门学科直接就叫「教育」。

senses.title: A level or stage of schooling
senses.titleCN: 某一阶段或层级的教育
senses.definition: a named stage such as primary, secondary or higher education
senses.definitionCN: 初等、中等或高等教育等具名阶段
senses.example: Fewer girls than boys continued into secondary education.
senses.exampleCN: 继续升入中等教育的女孩少于男孩。
senses.why: the single word covers each named stage, because a stage is only a portion of the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词覆盖每一个具名阶段，因为一个阶段只是整个过程中的一段。

senses.title: A public information campaign
senses.titleCN: 面向公众的宣传教育活动
senses.definition: an organized effort to teach the public about health, safety or civic matters
senses.definitionCN: 就健康、安全或公共事务向公众进行的有组织教育
senses.example: The clinic ran a road safety education week.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所办了一周的道路安全教育。
senses.why: the same word covers teaching that has no classroom, because the aim is still to change behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖没有教室的教学，因为目的仍是改变行为。

senses.title: The teaching profession and its work
senses.definition: the occupation of teachers and the professional work they do
senses.definitionCN: 教师的职业及其专业工作
senses.example: She entered education after ten years in engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工程界工作十年后进入教育行业。
senses.why: the activity became an industry with careers, so the word also names the trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动成为一个有职业路径的行业，因此这个词也指行业本身。

senses.title: The result: a cultivated mind
senses.titleCN: 教育的结果：被培养出的心智
senses.definition: the knowledge and judgement a person finally possesses as a result of learning
senses.definitionCN: 一个人因学习而最终拥有的知识与判断力
senses.example: His education showed in the way he listened before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他的教养体现在他先听后说的方式上。
senses.why: the word can name either the journey or what the traveller carries at the end.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指旅程，也可指旅人最终带着的东西。

intro.en: Education comes from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'to bring up, rear'. It reached English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 educatio「养育、培养」，其动词为 educare「抚养、培育」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is generally connected with the idea of drawing out a person's capacities, though the exact pre-Latin shape is not established.
items.cn: educare 意为「抚养、培育、养育」，一般认为与「把人身上的能力引发出来」这一观念相关，但其拉丁语之前的确切形态未获证明。

items.en: Educere, ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead', meant 'to lead out'. The famous notion of education as leading a mind out rests on this second verb.
items.cn: educere 由 ex-「向外」加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引出」。把教育理解为「把心智引出来」的著名说法，依据的正是这第二个动词。

items.en: Educatio named the rearing and training of a child. English took the noun through French with the same meaning.
items.cn: educatio 指对儿童的抚养与训练，英语经法语借入时保留了同一含义。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word increasingly meant formal instruction in schools rather than upbringing at home.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词越来越多地指学校里的正式教学，而非家庭中的养育。

items.en: In the twentieth century education also became the name of the academic discipline that studies teaching and learning.
items.cn: 二十世纪，「教育」又成为研究教与学的学科的正式名称。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the older verb meant 'nourish' or 'lead out' cannot be settled for the earliest layer, and the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to lead' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最早一层究竟取「养育」还是「引出」，无法定论；有人把它与表「引导」的词根相连，那只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name learning.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词衍生、极易混淆的词形；第二组是表示学习的近义词。

entries.definition: To teach or bring up someone; the noun education names the whole activity or system, not a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 指教育或培养某人；名词则指整个活动或体系，而非单个动作。

entries.definition: Meaning 'relating to education' or 'instructive', as in an educational visit.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与教育有关的」或「有教育意义的」，如一次有教育意义的参观。

entries.definition: Describes a person who has received education; it is a state, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述受过教育的人，是一种状态，而非体系。

entries.definition: A teacher or someone who works in education; the ending marks the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指教师或教育工作者，词尾标记施动者。

entries.definition: The formal instruction actually received in schools; it is the measurable part of education.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学校实际受到的正式教学，是教育中可测量的部分。

entries.definition: Practice aimed at a particular skill; it is narrower and usually has a task in view.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某项技能的练习，范围更窄，通常有具体任务。

entries.definition: The knowledge or skill acquired; it names the result rather than the organized giving.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得的知识或技能，说的是结果而非有组织的传授。

entries.definition: Deliberate teaching of content, often in steps; it is a method within education.
entries.definitionCN: 指有步骤地教授内容，是教育之内的种方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The family runs educate, educated, educational, educator, educative.
normal.cn: 同族包括「教育」「受过教育的」「教育的」「教育者」「有教育作用的」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: primary, secondary and higher education.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：初等、中等与高等教育。

normal.en: One verb has two readings, nourish and lead out, and both survive in how people talk about teaching.
normal.cn: 同一个动词有「养育」与「引出」两种读法，两种都留在人们谈论教学的方式里。

normal.en: The same noun serves the activity, the system and the discipline.
normal.cn: 同一个名词兼指活动、体系与学科。

normal.en: A classroom with a board, desks and books is the easiest picture to hold.
normal.cn: 有黑板、课桌与书本的教室是最容易抓住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp being lit rather than a bucket being filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被点亮，而不是一只桶被灌满。

abstract.en: Picture a seed given soil, water and time, then growing on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子得到土、水与时间，然后自行生长。

abstract.en: Picture a path with several gates, each opened by a different stage of study.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有几道门的路径，每道门由不同的学习阶段打开。

examples.en: Education is the surest route out of poverty for a whole village.
examples.cn: 对一个村庄来说，教育是摆脱贫困最可靠的路。

examples.en: The ministry spends a third of its budget on basic education.
examples.cn: 该部把三分之一的预算投入基础教育。

examples.en: Her education taught her to read a contract before signing it.
examples.cn: 她所受的教育让她在签字前先读懂合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱丢开心」——把不懂的东西一点点丢掉，心就开了，这就是教育。

root: 拉丁 educare「抚养、培育」构成 educatio「养育、训练」；一般认为它与表「引出」的 educere 相关，但「引出说」属后世解释，最早一层含义不能定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person is brought up, and that bringing-up is then organized into schools, stages, a profession and a discipline, until it finally names what the person carries away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个人被养成人，这种养成随后被组织成学校、阶段、职业与学科，最后用来指那个人带走的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp lit in a room rather than a bucket filled from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋里被点亮的一盏灯，而不是从外面灌满的一只桶。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS FRUIT: teaching is both the journey and the judgement carried home.
branches.cn: 动作与果实：教学既是旅程，也是带回家的判断力。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE TRADE: a system of schools needs a profession to run it.
branches.cn: 机器与行业：学校体系需要一支职业队伍来运转。

branches.en: BEFORE AND BEYOND SCHOOL: character is formed at home as much as in class.
branches.cn: 校门内外：性格在家里形成，不比在课堂上少。

branches.en: ORGANIZED KNOWLEDGE: a discipline studies education, while stages divide it.
branches.cn: 被组织起来的知识：一门学科研究教育，而阶段把教育分段。

branches.en: WITHOUT A CLASSROOM: campaigns teach the public where no desk exists.
branches.cn: 没有教室：宣传活动在无课桌处教育公众。

intro.en: The word is a Latin action noun whose verb also builds a compact English family, so it can be read from the verb outward.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动作名词，其动词在英语里也构成一个紧凑词族，因此可从动词向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin educare 'to rear' and educere 'to lead out' share the element ducere 'to lead'; educatio is the action noun built on the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 educare「养育」与 educere「引出」共享表「引导」的成分；educatio 是在前一个动词上构成的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix turns leading into a movement out of something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「引导」变成「从某处向外」的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a guide walking ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「引路者走在前面」的画面。

items.example: The verb names the whole work of raising a child.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指抚养孩子的全部工作。

items.example: They educate their children at home until six.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在六岁前由他们在家教育。

items.meaning: the act, system or result of teaching
items.example: Education changes what a family can imagine.
items.exampleCN: 教育改变一个家庭所能想象的东西。

items.example: The museum runs educational programs for schools.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆为学校开设教育项目。

items.example: The educator trained new teachers in the district.
items.exampleCN: 这位教育工作者在本区培训新教师。

items.example: Failure can be educative if it is examined.
items.exampleCN: 失败若被审视，也能起教育作用。

definition_zh: 包裹；包；一揽子方案；套餐；打包；包装
definition_en: something wrapped or boxed for sending and selling, a set of things or proposals offered together as one deal, or to put goods into a wrapper
core_image: 柜台上一只棕色纸包被麻绳十字捆紧，绳结压在正中间
scene: 快递站的塑料筐里堆着大小不一的纸箱，店员用胶带把最后一个封好。 The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.
sceneCN: 这里的 package 是「包裹」（第 1 个义项：包装好待寄送的东西）；句意为店员递给她一个用牛皮纸包好的沉包裹。图中可辨识物件：塑料筐、纸箱、胶带。

derivatives.zh: 由 package 去 e 加 -ing 构成，义为「包装材料；包装过程」
由 package 加 -er 构成，义为「打包商；节目或产品的制作方」
由前缀 pre-（预先）加 packaged 构成，义为「预先包装好的」

senses.title: Something wrapped for sending or selling
senses.definition: something wrapped in paper, plastic or a box so that it can be carried, sent or sold
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、塑料或盒子包好，便于携带、寄送或出售的东西
senses.example: The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.
senses.exampleCN: 店员递给她一个用牛皮纸包好的沉包裹。
senses.why: Package is pack plus the French ending -age, which names an action and its result, so the word means the outcome of packing: a thing tied up and sealed.
senses.whyCN: package 是 pack 加法语词尾 -age，这个后缀表示动作及其结果，所以这个词指「打包」的产物：一个被捆好、封好的东西。

senses.title: A set of things offered as one deal
senses.definition: several things, proposals or services put together and offered as a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 把若干东西、提议或服务合在一起，作为一个整体提供
senses.example: The government announced a package of measures to help small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 政府公布了一揽子帮助小企业的措施。
senses.why: If one wrapper can hold several objects, the same noun can hold several proposals under one agreement, which is how the word reached politics, tourism and software.
senses.whyCN: 既然一层包装能装下好几样东西，同一个名词就能把好几项提议装进一份协议里，这个词就是这样走进了政治、旅游与软件。

senses.title: To wrap goods for sale or sending
senses.definition: to put goods into a wrapper or a container, especially in a form suitable for selling
senses.definitionCN: 把货物装进包装物或容器，尤指做成适合出售的样子
senses.example: They packaged the biscuits in small foil bags.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把饼干装进小小的锡纸袋里。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of naming the thing already packed, it names the act of packing it, and modern marketing stretched it to designing the wrapper as well.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词翻了个面：不再指已经包好的东西，而指把它包起来这个动作；现代营销又把它扩展到包装的设计本身。

intro.en: Package is an English formation of the sixteenth century, made from the old noun pack and the French ending -age; the root pack is usually traced to Middle Dutch or Middle Low German, so the word is Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: package 是十六世纪英语自造的派生词，由古老名词 pack 与法语词尾 -age 构成；词根 pack 一般认为来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，因此这族词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: The noun pak meant a bundle tied up for carrying, and it is the usual source given for the English word pack.
items.cn: 名词 pak 指捆好便于搬运的包裹，通常被认为是英语 pack 的来源。

items.en: English took the noun as pack, a bundle or a load, and used it for goods tied together for a journey or a market.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词收作 pack，意为捆、一捆货，用来指为出行或赶集而捆在一起的货物。

items.en: The ending -age came into English through French from Latin -aticum and named an action or its result, as in voyage and baggage.
items.cn: 词尾 -age 经法语从拉丁语 -aticum 进入英语，表示动作或其结果，如 voyage 与 baggage。

items.en: Package first named both the act of packing and the bundle that resulted, and it soon covered goods prepared for a customer.
items.cn: package 最早同时指打包这个动作和打好的包，不久便用来指为顾客备好的货品。

items.en: Modern English adds package deal and package tour in trade and travel, the software package in computing, and the verb to package.
items.cn: 现代英语在商贸与旅游中加上 package deal 与 package tour，在计算机领域加上 software package，还发展出动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pack or on the same -age pattern; the near-meaning group collects words for wrapped goods and for bundles.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 pack 上或采用同一 -age 模式的词；近义组收表示包好的货物与捆扎之物的词。

entries.definition: To put things into a container, or a bundle of things.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西装进容器，或指一捆东西。

entries.definition: A small paper or plastic container, smaller than a package.
entries.definitionCN: 纸或塑料做的小容器，比 package 小得多。

entries.definition: The material in which goods are wrapped for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 商品出售时所用的包装材料。

entries.definition: The bags and cases a traveller carries.
entries.definitionCN: 旅行者携带的行李；与 package 共用 -age 词尾。

entries.definition: Something wrapped in paper and tied, especially for post.
entries.definitionCN: 用纸包好并捆上的东西，尤指邮寄的包裹。

entries.definition: A number of things tied or held together.
entries.definitionCN: 捆在一起或抱在一起的一堆东西。

entries.definition: A box made of cardboard.
entries.definitionCN: 纸板做的盒子；纸箱。

entries.definition: A load of goods sent to someone, especially for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 发运给某人的一批货物，尤指待售的货。

normalIntro.en: Package is the old word pack wearing the French ending -age, so the memory hooks follow the act of tying something up and the object that comes out of it.
normalIntro.cn: package 就是古老的 pack 披上法语词尾 -age，记忆钩子顺着「把东西捆起来」这个动作以及由此得到的物件走。

normal.en: Package is pack plus -age, the same ending that turns post into postage and bag into baggage.
normal.cn: package 是 pack 加 -age，同一个词尾把 post 变成 postage，把 bag 变成 baggage。

normal.en: A packet is the small cousin: both words grew from pack, but a packet is a little paper or plastic container, while a package can be as big as a carton.
normal.cn: packet 是它的小兄弟：两个词都从 pack 长出来，但 packet 是纸或塑料的小容器，而 package 可以大到一个纸箱。

normal.en: Package deal borrows the parcel picture: several items tied together and sold as one.
normal.cn: package deal 借用了包裹的画面：几样东西捆在一起，当作一件来卖。

normal.en: The verb adds nothing except the act, so packaged goods are simply goods that have been put into their wrappers.
normal.cn: 动词只添上动作本身，所以 packaged goods 不过是已经装进包装的货物。

normal.en: British speakers often say parcel for something sent by post, while package is the usual word in American English.
normal.cn: 英式英语常用 parcel 指邮寄的东西，而美式英语里 package 才是通常的说法。

abstract.en: A word that means a tied bundle keeps reminding us that selling often consists of deciding what to tie together.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「捆好的包」的词反复提醒人：所谓销售，常常就是决定把什么捆在一起。

abstract.en: A package deal hides its seams: the wrapping makes several separate things look like one decision.
abstract.cn: 一揽子交易藏起了接缝：包装让几件彼此独立的事看起来像同一个决定。

abstract.en: Wrapping protects a thing and also hides it, which is why the same word can mean care and concealment.
abstract.cn: 包装既保护一件东西，也遮住这件东西，所以同一个词既能表示用心，也能表示遮掩。

examples.en: The clerk handed her a heavy package wrapped in brown paper.
examples.cn: 店员递给她一个用牛皮纸包好的沉包裹。

examples.en: The government announced a package of measures to help small firms.
examples.cn: 政府公布了一揽子帮助小企业的措施。

examples.en: The company spent millions on packaging that can be recycled.
examples.cn: 这家公司花了大笔钱用于可回收的包装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派克吉」——派克把东西捆成一包再贴上标签；记住 package 是包裹、一揽子方案。

root: 由中古英语 pack（一捆，一般认为来自中古荷兰语或低地德语 pak）加法语词尾 -age（动作或结果）构成，十六世纪出现；词根属日耳曼语，无可靠的拉丁同族词，只有词尾 -age 经法语上溯拉丁语 -aticum。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bundle tied and sealed; the senses divide into the object itself, a set of things sold under one wrapping, and the act of wrapping them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个捆好封好的包；义项按「包本身」「包在同一层包装里的一套东西」「把它们包起来的动作」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown paper parcel crossed by twine, the knot pressed flat in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上一只棕色纸包被麻绳十字捆紧，绳结压在正中间。

branches.en: a parcel pushed across a counter

branches.en: a carton sealed with tape before a van leaves
branches.cn: 货车出发前用胶带封好的纸箱

branches.en: a list of measures signed as one document
branches.cn: 作为一份文件签署的一组措施

branches.en: a holiday whose flight and hotel are sold together

branches.en: hands folding foil around a row of biscuits
branches.cn: 双手把锡纸裹在一排饼干上

intro.en: The word is an old Germanic noun for a bundle wearing a French noun ending, so its parts still say a packed thing and the result of packing.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个意为「捆」的古老日耳曼名词，披着法语名词词尾，各部分至今仍在说「被捆好的东西」与「打包的结果」。

latinIntro.en: The root pack has no reliable Latin cognate; only the noun ending -age reached English through French from Latin -aticum, so no Latin word is listed for the root itself.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 pack 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；只有名词词尾 -age 经法语上溯拉丁语 -aticum，因此词根本身不列拉丁词。

scene: 这座桥有七十年的历史。 The bridge is seventy years old.

senses.title: The number seventy
senses.definition: the number equal to seven times ten
senses.definitionCN: 等于七乘十的数字
senses.example: The bridge is seventy years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥有七十年的历史。
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.

items.en: Seventy also named groups and ages.

normalIntro.en: Seventy is seven tens, a number often linked to long experience.
normalIntro.cn: seventy 是七个十，常与漫长的经历联系在一起。

normal.en: The old tree is seventy years old.

abstract.en: Age is a measure, not a limit.

branches.en: Counting years is still counting.
branches.cn: 数年岁，仍然是在数数。

intro.en: Seventy joins seven to the tens suffix -ty.
intro.cn: seventy 把 seven 与表示十的倍数的后缀 -ty 连接起来。

latinIntro.en: Seventy has no Latin ancestor; Latin septuaginta is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: seventy 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 septuaginta（七十）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The building dates from the seventies.

items.exampleCN: 人们庆祝了他们的第七十年。
这是一个七十年的传统。

definition_zh: 一次；曾经；一…就；一旦
definition_en: one single time; at some time in the past; as soon as; if ever, used to introduce a condition
core_image: 一枚只用过一次的票根，用过就被撕下丢进铁盒
scene: 抽屉最深处的铁盒里压着一张旧票根，边角磨得发白，纸上的字迹早已认不出。 She once lived in this old house beside the river.
sceneCN: 这里 once 是「曾经、从前」（第 2 个义项：过去某个不确定的时期）；句意是她曾在这栋河边老屋里住过。画面是压着旧票根的铁盒与磨白的纸角。

derivatives.zh: 由 once 与 over 复合而成，义为「匆匆的一瞥；粗略的检查」
由 once 与 in a lifetime 组合而成，义为「一生只有一次的」

senses.title: One single time and no more
senses.definition: one time, and no more than one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次，而且仅只一次
senses.example: I met her once at a conference in Shanghai.
senses.exampleCN: 我在上海的一次会议上见过她一面。
senses.why: The Old English form was a genitive of the word for one, so the count starts at a single occasion and stops there.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式是「一」这个词的属格，所以计数从单独一次开始，也就到此为止。

senses.title: At some time in the past
senses.definition: at an unspecified time in the past, especially a period that is now over
senses.definitionCN: 在过去某个不确定的时期，尤指已经结束的一段时光
senses.example: He once worked as a night guard in a paper mill.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾在造纸厂当过夜班保安。
senses.why: A single occasion placed far enough back in memory stops being a count and becomes a period that once existed, which is how the word turns into formerly.
senses.whyCN: 单独一次被推到记忆深处，就不再是计数，而成了曾经存在过的一段日子，词义于是转为「从前」。

senses.title: As soon as; at the moment that
senses.definition: as soon as something happens, something else happens or becomes true
senses.definitionCN: 某事刚一发生，另一件事就随之发生或成立
senses.example: Once the rain stopped, the whole street came out to dry its washing.
senses.exampleCN: 雨一停，整条街的人就出来晾衣服。
senses.why: The count shrinks to a single moment, and that moment of time becomes the hinge on which the next event turns.
senses.whyCN: 计数收窄到一个瞬间，而时间上的那一刻正成了下一件事转动的铰链。

senses.title: If ever; whenever a condition holds
senses.definition: used to introduce a condition: if something ever happens or is true, the main clause follows
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出条件：只要某事发生或成立，后面的结果就随之而来
senses.example: Once you sign the form, the offer cannot be withdrawn.
senses.exampleCN: 你一旦签了这张表，这个录用条件就不能撤回。
senses.why: From the moment that to provided that is a short step, because a single moment can also mark the point where a condition takes effect.
senses.whyCN: 从「就在那一刻」到「只要」只有一小步，因为单独的那一刻也可以标出条件开始生效的位置。

intro.en: Once is a frozen genitive of the Old English word for one, and it has kept the meaning of a single occasion for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: once 是古英语「一」这个词属格形式的凝固，一千多年来一直保留「一次」的含义。

items.en: The numeral an meant one, and its genitive anes meant of one, which is the source of the modern word.
items.cn: 数词 an 意为「一」，它的属格 anes 意为「之一的」，正是现代 once 的来源。

items.en: In early English anes worked as an adverb for one time, and its final s was gradually absorbed into the spoken form.
items.cn: 在早期英语中，anes 作副词表示「一次」，词尾的 s 逐渐被口语形式吸收。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as ones and once competed, and once won because it matched the pattern of twice.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ones 与 once 等拼法并存，once 最终胜出，因为它与 twice 的构词方式相合。

items.en: By the sixteenth century once had also become a conjunction meaning as soon as, turning a count of times into a point in time.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，once 又发展出连词用法，表示「一…就」，把次数扩展为时间上的一个点。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adverb of counting and the conjunction of condition, and once also lives inside fixed phrases such as at once and once more.
items.cn: 现代英语保留计数的副词与表条件的连词，once 也活在 at once、once more 这类固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words built on the same count of one; the near-meaning group gathers words for a former time and for every time that something happens.
note.cn: 形近组收同样从「一」出发构成的词；近义组收表示从前某个时期以及每当某事发生时的词。

entries.definition: Two times, built with the same -ce ending as once.
entries.definitionCN: 两次，与 once 共用同样的词尾 -ce。

entries.definition: The numeral at the base of once, still used for a single thing or person.
entries.definitionCN: once 所依托的数词，至今表示单独的一件或一人。

entries.definition: A word for the present occasion, from a different phrase; it looks close to once but was formed separately.
entries.definitionCN: 指「眼下这一回」的词，来源是另一个短语，拼写与 once 相近但构词独立。

entries.definition: A unit of weight from Latin uncia; only the opening sound resembles once.
entries.definitionCN: 源自拉丁语 uncia 的重量单位，只有开头的音与 once 相近。

entries.definition: At an earlier time; in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 从前；以前。

entries.definition: Before the present time or before a stated event.
entries.definitionCN: 先前；在所述事件之前。

entries.definition: Every time that; at any time that.
entries.definitionCN: 每当；无论何时。

entries.definition: Immediately at the moment that something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 一…就；在某事发生的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: The word is a frozen count of one, and its family keeps returning to a single occasion, a single past period and a single moment that starts something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一」的凝固计数，同族用法反复回到单独一次、单独一段过去，以及开启某事的单独一刻。

normal.en: The Old English genitive anes meant of one, so once is literally a count of one occasion.
normal.cn: 古英语属格 anes 意为「之一的」，所以 once 字面上就是数一次。

normal.en: Once and twice share the ending -ce, which is why the two words sound like a matched pair.
normal.cn: once 与 twice 共用词尾 -ce，所以两个词听起来像成对的。

normal.en: At once means at one moment, and that is how a count turns into immediacy.
normal.cn: at once 意为「就在一刻」，计数就是这样转成「立刻」。

normal.en: Once as a conjunction marks the single moment when something begins, and English glosses it as as soon as.
normal.cn: once 作连词时标出某事开始的那一瞬间，英语用 as soon as 来解释它。

normal.en: For once stresses that the single occasion is unusual rather than the usual pattern.
normal.cn: for once 强调这一次不同寻常，而不是一贯如此。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket torn in half after one ride: the stub left in the box is the whole of the word once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张车票在一次行程后被撕成两半：留在盒里的票根就是 once 的全部含义。

abstract.en: A single second on a clock face can set everything else moving, and that second is once standing at the head of a clause.
abstract.cn: 钟面上单独的一秒能让之后的一切动起来，而这一秒就是站在小句开头的 once。

abstract.en: Memory turns one distant occasion into the softer word once, the way a photograph outlives the day it was taken.
abstract.cn: 记忆把遥远的一次变成语气更柔的 once，就像照片比拍摄的那一天活得更久。

examples.en: I met her once at a conference in Shanghai.
examples.cn: 我在上海的一次会议上见过她一面。

examples.en: He once worked as a night guard in a paper mill.
examples.cn: 他曾在造纸厂当过夜班保安。

examples.en: Once the rain stopped, the whole street came out to dry its washing.
examples.cn: 雨一停，整条街的人就出来晾衣服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「万思」——万千思绪只此一回；once 是一次，也是曾经。

root: 古英语数词 an（一）的属格形式 anes 凝固成副词，意为「一次」；词尾与 twice 的 -ce 相合，后又引申出「曾经」与连词「一…就、一旦」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a count that stops at one; the senses spread from a single occasion to a distant occasion and to the single moment at which something begins.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「数到一就停」；义项从单独一次，扩展到遥远的某一次，再到某事开始的那一瞬间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ticket stub torn off after one single use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚用过一次就被撕下的票根。

branches.en: a ticket torn after one ride
branches.cn: 一次车程后被撕开的票

branches.en: an old man describing the mill where he worked as a youth
branches.cn: 老人说起年轻时做工的那家造纸厂

branches.en: one occasion that lies either today or long ago
branches.cn: 同一次经历，或在今天，或在很久以前

branches.en: the rain stopping and the street filling with people
branches.cn: 雨停之后街上涌出的人群

branches.en: a signature that locks an offer in place
branches.cn: 一个签名把录用条件锁定

intro.en: The word is held together by the Old English numeral for one, its genitive ending, and the frozen adverb that grew out of them.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语数词「一」、它的属格词尾，以及由二者凝固而成的副词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: frozen genitive ending, as in twice
items.meaningCN: 凝固的属格词尾，与 twice 同型

items.meaning: immediately, or all at the same moment

definition_zh: 笔记；便条；音符；注意；记下
definition_en: a short written record or message; a single musical sound; attention; and the act of noticing or writing something down
core_image: 纸页边缘写满小字，一张折好的短笺压在书页之间
scene: 厨房的桌上压着一张折好的纸条，字迹很急，末尾没有署名。 She read the note twice before answering.
sceneCN: 这里是「便条、短笺」（第 2 个义项：写在纸上的简短留言），句意为她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。图中可辨识物件：折好的纸条、厨房桌、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 note 与 book 复合而成，义为「笔记本」
由 note 的拉丁词干加 -able 构成，义为「值得注意的；显著的」
由拉丁词干 notare 加 -tion 构成，义为「记号系统；记谱法」

senses.title: A short written record of something heard or read
senses.definition: a short written record, especially of what a speaker said or what a reader wants to remember
senses.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，尤指记下讲者所说或读者想记住的内容
senses.example: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。
senses.why: Latin nota was a mark or written sign, and the first English sense kept that idea of a small written trace left behind for later use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nota 是「记号、写下的符号」，英语最初的意思保留了这种「为以后使用而留下的小小书写痕迹」。

senses.title: A short written message
senses.definition: a short informal letter or message written on a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 写在纸上的简短、非正式的留言或信
senses.example: She read the note twice before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。
senses.why: Because any written mark can be handed to someone else, note slid from a private record to a message left for another person, usually brief and casual.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何书写记号都能交给别人，note 就从私人记录滑向留给别人的留言，通常简短而随意。

senses.title: A single musical sound or its written sign
senses.definition: a single sound in music, or the written symbol that stands for it
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中的单个音，或代表这个音的书写符号
senses.example: She held the last note longer than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最后一个音拖得比别的音更长。
senses.why: A musical tone can be written down like any other sign, so the word for a written mark came to name one printed dot on a staff and then the sound it stands for.
senses.whyCN: 乐音也能像别的符号一样写下来，于是表示书写记号的词先指谱线中的一个点，再指它所代表的那个音。

senses.title: Attention or notice given to something
senses.definition: attention given to something, especially in the phrase take note of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给予的关注，尤用于 take note of 这一说法
senses.example: Take note of the small changes in the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 请留意这个图案里细微的变化。
senses.why: A note is something you write so that it will be remembered, and from that comes the sense of giving something enough attention for it to be remembered.
senses.whyCN: 笔记是为了日后记得才写下的东西，由此引申出「给予足够关注、以便记住」的意思。

senses.title: To notice or write something down
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, or to write it down so that it is recorded
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，或把它写下来留作记录
senses.example: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。
senses.why: Once the noun means a written trace of attention, the matching verb naturally means the act that produces it, so noting is both watching closely and setting the result on paper.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已经表示「注意力留下的书写痕迹」，与之对应的动词自然就表示产生这个痕迹的动作，所以 noting 既是仔细观察，也是把结果落到纸上。

intro.en: Note comes from a Latin word for a mark or written sign, entered English through Old French, and later grew senses for messages, music and attention.
intro.cn: note 来自拉丁语中表示「记号、书写符号」的词，经古法语进入英语，后来才长出留言、音乐与注意等义项。

items.en: Nota was a mark, a written character or a sign of something, and it is generally connected with the Latin verb for knowing, noscere.
items.cn: nota 是记号、书写符号或某事的标志，一般认为它与拉丁语中表示「认识」的动词 noscere 有关。

items.en: The verb notare meant to mark, to write down or to observe, and it supplied the family of words about noting and notation.
items.cn: 动词 notare 意为标记、写下或观察，由此衍生出与记录和记号系统有关的一族词。

items.en: Old French passed on note as a written mark, a memorandum or a short writing after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，古法语把 note 传进英语，意思为书面的记号、备忘或短小的文字。

items.en: Middle English note covered a written record, a melody and a token of something, so the musical sense was already present.
items.cn: 中古英语的 note 已包含书面记录、曲调与某事物的标志，音乐义那时就已经在场。

items.en: Modern English adds the short message, the musical symbol, the sense of attention and the verb, together with the compound banknote for paper money.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了便条、音乐符号、注意等意思和动词用法，还添上表示纸币的复合词 banknote。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem nota through English derivatives; the near-meaning group collects the short writings and messages that note resembles.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 nota 收英语派生词；近义组收与 note 相近的短小文字与留言。

entries.definition: A system of written symbols, such as the notation used for music.
entries.definitionCN: 书写符号的系统，如音乐所用的记谱法。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention, built from the same stem with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的，同一词干加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for writing notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记笔记、带空白页的本子。

entries.definition: A short written message inside an office or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 办公室或机构内部简短的书面留言。

entries.definition: Information sent from one person to another, in speech, writing or another medium.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人传给另一人的信息，可用口头、书面或其他方式。

entries.definition: A written or stored account of something kept for later reference.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而保存的书面或存储记载。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin mark that became a small piece of writing, then a message, a musical sign and a act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原是拉丁语的「记号」，后来变成一小段文字、一条留言、一个音乐符号，以及一次关注的动作。

normal.en: Latin nota meant a mark or written sign, so every sense of note still involves something set down to be seen again.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为记号或书写符号，所以 note 的每个义项都离不开「写下来以便再看」这件事。

normal.en: Notare is the Latin verb to mark or write, and it is the base of notation and notable.
normal.cn: notare 是拉丁语里「标记、书写」的动词，也是 notation 与 notable 的底座。

normal.en: The musical note is simply a written sign on a staff, which is why the same word names the symbol and the sound.
normal.cn: 音乐里的 note 不过是谱线上的一个书写符号，所以同一个词既指符号也指声音。

normal.en: Take note of keeps the physical picture: you write something because you want to keep it in mind.
normal.cn: take note of 保留了那个具体画面：你把它写下来，是因为想把它记在心里。

normal.en: Banknote is a note in the old sense of a written promise to pay, now the paper money itself.
normal.cn: banknote 里的 note 用的是旧义「书面的付款承诺」，今天则直接指那张纸币。

abstract.en: A mark that was meant to be read later became a message meant for someone else, and both still depend on paper holding a thought still.
abstract.cn: 一个本来留给以后自己看的记号，变成了留给别人的留言，两者都依赖纸张把一个念头固定住。

abstract.en: Note shows how writing turns attention into an object: what you noticed becomes something you can hand over.
abstract.cn: note 展示了书写如何把注意力变成物件：你注意到的东西变成可以递交出去的东西。

abstract.en: The same short word can be a page of study, a line of music and a warning, because all three are traces left for a later reader.
abstract.cn: 同一个短词可以是整页的学习、一行音乐，也可以是一句提醒，因为三者都是留给后来读者看的痕迹。

examples.en: She read the note twice before answering.
examples.cn: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。

examples.en: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。

examples.en: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特」——桌上压着一张小纸条，几行字就说明了来意；note 就是便条、笔记。

root: 拉丁语 nota（记号、书写符号）与动词 notare（标记、写下），经古法语 note 进入中古英语；同族词有 notable、notation、notebook。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written mark kept for later; the senses then divide into the record, the message, the musical sign, and attention with its verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为日后而留下的书写记号」；义项由此分出记录、留言、音乐符号，以及注意和相应的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page crowded with small handwriting, with a folded slip pressed between the leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满小字的纸页，夹着一张折好的短笺。

branches.en: a page of lecture notes written in a tight hand
branches.cn: 写得密密麻麻的一页讲座笔记

branches.en: a sentence underlined twice in the margin
branches.cn: 页边被划了两道线的句子

branches.en: a folded slip left on a kitchen table
branches.cn: 厨房桌上留下的折好的纸条

branches.en: one held tone at the end of a song
branches.cn: 歌曲结尾一个被拖长的音

branches.en: a reader pausing, then writing a date in the corner
branches.cn: 读者停了一下，在角上写下日期

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for a mark, its verb, and English endings that build its derivatives and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语表示「记号」的名词与动词上，再由英语词尾构成它的派生词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun nota and its verb notare are the recorded source of this word family, so the Latin entries below are its direct ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 nota 与动词 notare 是这个词族有记录的来源，因此下面的拉丁词条是它的直系祖先。

definition_zh: 水池；水洼；游泳池；共用资源；公摊资金；集中；凑集；台球
definition_en: a small area of still water, a basin built for swimming, a shared supply of money or people, the act of gathering such things, and a table game played with cues
core_image: 散落各处的零钱被一只手拢成一堆，旁边的水面平得像一面镜子
scene: 夏天的午后，水面被阳光照得发亮，孩子们扶着浮板在浅水区排队。 The hotel pool was crowded with families escaping the heat.
sceneCN: 这里的 pool 是「游泳池」（第 2 个义项：供游泳的水池）；句意为旅馆的泳池里挤满了来避暑的家庭。图中可辨识物件：浮板、池边扶手、水面反光。

pos.zh: 水池；水洼；游泳池；共用资源；台球

derivatives.zh: 由 pool 加 -ing 构成，义为「集中；合并（资源）」
由 pool 与 side 复合而成，义为「池边」
由 car 与 pool 复合而成，义为「拼车；合用车辆」

senses.title: A small body of still water
senses.definition: a small area of still water, either left by rain or made by people
senses.definitionCN: 一小片不流动的水，或由雨水积成，或由人工砌成
senses.example: Rainwater collected in a shallow pool beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水在路边积成了一个浅浅的水洼。
senses.why: Old English pol named still water and the deep spots in a river, so the word starts from water that stays put instead of running on.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pol 指静水以及河中的深水处，所以这个词的起点是不往前流、留在原地的水。

senses.title: A basin built for swimming
senses.definition: an artificial basin filled with water and used for swimming
senses.definitionCN: 灌满水、供人游泳的人工水池
senses.example: The children swam in the hotel pool all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们整个下午都在旅馆的泳池里游泳。
senses.why: A pool is water held in one place, so a basin built to hold it for swimming needs no new word, only a purpose added in front.
senses.whyCN: pool 本来就是蓄在一处的水，因此供游泳的水池不必另造新词，只需在前面加一个用途。

senses.title: A shared supply of money or people
senses.definition: an amount of money, work or people contributed by many and used by all of them
senses.definitionCN: 由多方拿出、供大家共同使用的钱、工作或人力
senses.example: The company draws from a large pool of engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从庞大的人才库中选用工程师。
senses.why: The game sense came from French poule, a common stake, and that shared pot of money gave English the idea of any supply that many people pay into and draw from.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自法语 poule（大家押下的赌注），那口公用的钱罐让英语引申出「众人凑入、众人取用」的资源。

senses.title: To gather things into one shared whole
senses.definition: to put money, effort or equipment together so that a group can use it
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、力气或设备合在一起，供一群人共同使用
senses.example: The two firms pooled their resources to finish the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司集中资源，才把这座桥修完。
senses.why: If a pool is a common pot, the verb is simply the act of filling it: each side drops something in before anyone draws anything out.
senses.whyCN: 如果 pool 是一口公用的罐子，动词就是往罐里放东西的动作：各方先各放一点，之后才谈取用。

senses.title: A table game played with cues
senses.definition: a game played on a cloth-covered table in which balls are struck with a long cue
senses.definitionCN: 在铺布球台上用长杆击球的游戏
senses.example: They spent the evening playing pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打了一晚上台球。
senses.why: In French poule the stakes were pooled before play, and the table game kept the name of that shared bet rather than any word for water.
senses.whyCN: 法语 poule 指开局前把赌注合在一起，这种球戏留下的是「公共赌注」的名字，与水毫无关系。

intro.en: Pool has two streams: an Old English word for still water, and a French word for a common stake that gave English the shared-fund and billiard senses.
intro.cn: pool 有两条来路：一条是古英语中表示静水的词，另一条是法语中表示公共赌注的词，后者带来「共用资金」与「台球」两个义项。

items.en: Old English pol meant a small body of water and could also name a deep, slow spot in a river.
items.cn: 古英语的 pol 指一小片水，也可指河中水深流缓的地方。

items.en: Related forms appear in Middle Dutch poel and Old High German pfuol, but the earlier origin of the set is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 poel 与古高地德语 pfuol 有相关形式，但这组词更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English pool broadened to ponds, mill dams and any still water, natural or dug.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pool 扩展到池塘、磨坊水坝以及任何静水，无论天然还是人工。

items.en: French poule, literally a hen, named the stakes that card players put into one pot, and English borrowed the word for that common fund.
items.cn: 法语 poule 本义是母鸡，用来指牌戏玩家押进同一口罐子的赌注，英语借来表示这笔公共的钱。

items.en: From card tables the shared-fund sense spread to typing pools and car pools, while the cue game kept the name of the pooled stakes.
items.cn: 从牌桌出发，「公共资金」义扩展到打字员组、拼车等说法，而用球杆玩的游戏则留下了「公共赌注」这个名字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers one-syllable words that differ from pool by a letter; the near-meaning group gathers other containers and bodies of water.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pool 只差一个字母的单音节词；近义组收其他盛水之处与水体。

entries.definitionCN: 细长的杆；地球的两极。

entries.definition: A survey of people's opinions, or the counting of votes.

entries.definition: A dog with thick curly hair, often clipped in a fancy style.

entries.definitionCN: 地面上由雨水积成的小浅水洼。

entries.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.

entries.definition: A wide open container for water, or a hollow area of land.

entries.definition: A large artificial lake used for storing water.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蓄水的大型人工湖；水库。

normalIntro.en: Pool joins two old ideas, still water and a common stake, and almost every sense can be reached from one of them.
normalIntro.cn: pool 把两个古老的意思合在一起：静水与公共赌注；几乎每个义项都能从其中之一走到。

normal.en: Old English pol meant still water and a deep spot in a river, which is why the water senses need no explanation.
normal.cn: 古英语 pol 指静水与河中的深水处，所以与水有关的义项不需要额外解释。

normal.en: French poule literally means hen; it named the stakes players pushed into one pot, and that pot became the shared fund.
normal.cn: 法语 poule 本义是母鸡，指玩家押进同一口罐子的赌注，这口罐子后来成了共用资金。

normal.en: A talent pool and a gene pool both use the image of a common supply that people or traits are drawn from.
normal.cn: talent pool 与 gene pool 用的都是「公共储备」这个意象，人或性状从中取用。

normal.en: Pool resources is the verb built from the pot: put in first, take out later, and the group gains what no one had alone.
normal.cn: pool resources 是从那口罐子来的动词：先放进去，后面再取，群体便得到了单个人没有的东西。

normal.en: Pool table keeps the gambling name, not the water name, which is why billiards has nothing to do with swimming.
normal.cn: pool table 保留的是赌博的名字，不是水的名字，所以台球与游泳无关。

abstract.en: Water that stops moving and money that stops circulating in private hands follow the same shape: something gathered into one place.
abstract.cn: 停止流动的水，与不再留在私人手里的钱，形状相同：都是被聚到一处的东西。

abstract.en: A pool is a promise that what is put in will be shared out, whether it holds water, money or engineers.
abstract.cn: pool 是一种承诺：放进去的东西会被分用，无论里面装的是水、钱还是工程师。

abstract.en: Two unrelated histories meeting in one spelling is a reminder that a word can carry more than one memory.
abstract.cn: 两段毫不相干的历史挤进同一个拼写，提醒人一个词可以同时带着不止一段记忆。

examples.cn: 雨水在路边积成了一个浅浅的水洼。

examples.cn: 两家公司集中资源，才把这座桥修完。

sensesIntro.en: The core is water held in one place; the branches add what the water is for, then move to the separate French sense of a common pot of money.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是蓄在一处的水；各分支先补出水用来做什么，再转到法语来的另一条线——公共的钱罐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: still water held inside a rim, and coins pushed into one common pot.
core.cn: 核心意象：被边沿围住的一汪静水，以及被拢进同一口罐子的硬币。

branches.en: rainwater sitting in a hollow after a storm
branches.cn: 暴雨后积在凹处的一洼雨水

branches.en: lanes and a starting block under bright water
branches.cn: 明亮的池水下，泳道与出发台

branches.en: coins dropped into one pot before a card game
branches.cn: 牌局开始前投进同一口罐子的硬币

intro.en: The word is held together by one Old English noun for still water and a set of modern compounds that name the basin, its users and its games.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示静水的古英语名词，加上一组指水池、使用者与球戏的现代复合词共同支撑。

definition_zh: 在……下面；低于；在下面；下文
definition_en: in or to a lower position than something, or less than a particular amount
core_image: 一张桌子的桌面，和桌面下方的那片地板
scene: 潜水员透过舷窗看见一条小鱼慢慢地游过去。 A small fish swam below the boat.
sceneCN: 这里 below 是「在……下面」（第 1 个义项：位置低于某物）；句意为一条小鱼在船下游过。

derivatives.zh: 同源基础词，义为「低的」，是 below 的后半部分来源
由 low 加 -er 构成，义为「较低的」，也可作动词表示「降低」

senses.title: In a lower position
senses.definition: in or to a position that is lower than something else
senses.definitionCN: 在比另一物体更低的位置，或向这样的位置
senses.example: A small fish swam below the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小鱼在船下游过。
senses.why: The word is be-, meaning at, plus low, so it literally says at a low place, and that is the oldest and clearest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 be-「在」加 low「低」，字面就是「在较低处」，这也是最古老、最清楚的义项。

senses.title: Less than an amount or level
senses.definition: less than a particular number, temperature, standard, or level
senses.definitionCN: 少于某个数字、温度、标准或水平
senses.example: The temperature fell below zero.
senses.exampleCN: 气温降到零度以下。
senses.why: A number on a scale sits above or below another just as an object sits above or below a table, so the place picture turns into the sense of less than.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上的数字像物体在桌面上下的位置一样，也分上下，于是位置画面转成「少于」的意思。

senses.title: At a lower place, standing alone
senses.definition: used as an adverb for something located lower, without an object
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，不带宾语，指位于较低处的东西
senses.example: From the hill we could see the town below.
senses.exampleCN: 从山上我们能看见下面的小镇。
senses.why: With the object dropped, the word still points downward and now simply describes what lies lower than the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 去掉宾语后，这个词仍指下方，只是单纯描述比说话人更低的东西。

senses.title: Further down a page
senses.definition: further down on a page or in a text, used to point readers to later material
senses.definitionCN: 在书页或文本中更靠下的位置，用来指引读者看后面的内容
senses.example: Please read the notes below.
senses.exampleCN: 请读下面的注释。
senses.why: A page is also a vertical space, so the part lower on the page is the part below, and the word came to mean further in the text.
senses.whyCN: 书页本身也是一个竖直的空间，页面上更靠下的一段就是 below，于是这个词也表示「文本更后面」。

intro.en: Below is a compound of be- and low, and it later displaced older English words for the same idea.
intro.cn: below 是 be- 与 low 的复合词，后来取代了英语里几个表示同一意思的旧词。

items.en: Middle English formed the word from be-, meaning at, and low, meaning low.
items.cn: 中古英语用 be-「在」与 low「低」造出这个词。

items.en: The prefix placed the whole word in a spot rather than in a direction.
items.cn: 这个前缀把整个词落在某个位置上，而不只是表示方向。

items.en: Low came from an old Germanic adjective for a flat or low position, and it is still the everyday word.
items.cn: low 来自古老的日耳曼语形容词，表示平坦或低的位置，今天仍是日常用词。

items.en: Old English used other words such as beneothan for below, and the modern form won out only later.
items.cn: 古英语另有 beneothan 等词表示「在下面」，现代形式是后来才胜出的。

items.en: From place the word spread to amounts, standards, and the lower part of a page.
items.cn: 从位置出发，这个词扩展到数量、标准以及书页的下半部分。

items.en: Today below works as a preposition and an adverb, and it often appears in written instructions.
items.cn: 今天 below 可作介词和副词，常出现在书面说明中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects low-family words and similar-sounding forms; the near-meaning group collects other words for a lower position.
note.cn: 形近组收 low 词族的词与读音相近的形式；近义组收其他表示「下方」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a small height, the second half of below.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「低的」，是 below 的后半部分来源。

entries.definition: The comparative of low, or a verb meaning to bring down.
entries.definitionCN: low 的比较级，也可作动词表示「降低」。

entries.definition: To shout loudly and deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「大声吼叫」，词尾读音与 below 相近。

entries.definition: To send air out, or a stroke; it sounds close to below.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吹」，也可作名词指「一击」，读音与 below 接近。

entries.definition: Directly beneath something, often covered by it.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……正下方」，常含被覆盖之意。

entries.definition: Under or lower than something, a more literary word.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……下面」，是较文的用词。

entries.definition: Directly under and usually hidden by something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……底下」，通常含被遮住之意。

entries.definition: At a higher position; the direct opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……上面」，是第一个义项的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded compound parts, the real low family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、真实的 low 词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- means at and low means low, so below simply says at a low place.
normal.cn: be- 表示「在」，low 表示「低」，所以 below 就是「在较低处」。

normal.en: Low, lower and below all keep the same height picture.
normal.cn: low、lower、below 都保留同一个「高低」画面。

normal.en: On a page, the lower part is also called below, which is why notes are below.
normal.cn: 在书页上，靠下的部分也叫 below，所以注释总在「下面」。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with zero, average, surface and below.
normal.cn: 它常与 zero、average、surface 搭配，也见于 see below。

normal.en: Spell b-e-l-o-w: be plus low, with the ow at the end.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-l-o-w：be 加 low，结尾是 ow。

abstract.en: See a tabletop and the floor under it: the gap itself is below.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面和桌面下方的地板，中间那一块就是 below。

abstract.en: Turn the same picture into a thermometer and then into a page: height becomes number, then position in text.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画换成温度计，再换成书页：高度先变成数字，再变成文中的位置。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the floor under the table bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让桌面下的地板把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 一条小鱼在船下游过。

examples.en: The temperature fell below zero.
examples.cn: 气温降到零度以下。

examples.en: Please read the notes below.
examples.cn: 请读下面的注释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必漏」——水必漏到桌子下面去：在……下面

root: below 由 be-「在」与 low「低」合成，字面就是「在较低处」。它在中古英语成形，逐渐取代了 beneothan 等旧说法。由「位置低」引申出「数量、水平低于」，也能单独作副词；书页靠下的一段同样叫 below，因此可以表示「见下文」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of below stay on one vertical line: lower than a thing, lower than a number, lower than the speaker, lower on a page.
sensesIntro.cn: below 的四个义项都留在同一条竖直线上：比物体低、比数字低、比说话人低、在页面上更靠下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tabletop and the floor beneath it
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子的桌面和桌面下方的地板

branches.en: THE PLACE: the plainest sense is a spot lower than an object.
branches.cn: 位置线：最朴素的义项就是比某物更低的地方。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a number lower on a scale becomes less than a level.
branches.cn: 刻度线：刻度上更低的数字变成「少于某个水平」。

branches.en: THE VIEW: with no object the word describes whatever lies lower in sight.
branches.cn: 视野线：不带宾语时，这个词描述视野中更低的东西。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the lower part of a page becomes the later part of a text.
branches.cn: 页面线：书页靠下的部分变成文本更靠后的部分。

branches.en: THE SAME AXIS: space and number share one vertical picture of high and low.
branches.cn: 同一轴线：空间与数字共用一幅「上下」的竖直画面。

intro.en: Below is a fused compound of be- and low; the items below are those parts and the words built on low.
intro.cn: below 是 be- 与 low 的粘合复合词，下面列出的是这些成分以及建立在 low 之上的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin infra and sub are recorded words for below and under; they are parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 infra 与 sub 分别表示「在……下面」和「在……之下」，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

definition_zh: 紧张的；焦虑的；神经的；易激动的；神经质的
definition_en: anxious and easily worried; relating to the nerves of the body; highly strung and quick to react
core_image: 考场门口，一个女生反复整理袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的门
scene: 考前的走廊里，一个女生站在门口，手指一遍遍捏着袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的教室门。 She felt nervous before the oral exam, so she kept checking her notes.
sceneCN: 这里是「紧张的、焦虑的」（第 1 个义项：面对考验时心里不安）；句意为口试之前她感到紧张，所以不停地看笔记。图中可辨识物件：走廊、袖口、教室门。

pos.zh: 紧张的；焦虑的；神经的；易激动的；神经质的

由 nervous 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧张；神经质」
nervous 的词根，义为「神经；勇气」

senses.title: Anxious and unable to relax
senses.definition: worried and unable to relax because something important or uncertain is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 因为重要或不确定的事即将发生而担心、无法放松
senses.example: She felt nervous before the oral exam, so she kept checking her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 口试之前她感到紧张，所以不停地看笔记。
senses.why: The word born from sinews came to describe a body whose threads are pulled tight; English then read that tightness as worry, so a physical tension became the ordinary word for anxiety.
senses.whyCN: 这个从「筋」生出的词，后来形容身体里一根根线被拉紧的状态；英语又把这种紧绷读成担忧，于是身体的紧张成了日常表示焦虑的词。

senses.title: Relating to the nerves of the body
senses.definition: connected with the fibres and tissue that carry signals in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与体内传递信号的纤维和组织有关的
senses.example: Nervous tissue carries signals from the skin to the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 神经组织把信号从皮肤传到大脑。
senses.why: This sense is the oldest technical one, because the adjective was formed directly from the noun for a bodily cord; anatomy never lost the word, even after everyday speech took it over for worry.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项是最早的技术义，因为形容词直接由表示身体细索的名词构成；即使日常口语把这个词拿去表示担忧，解剖学也从未丢掉它。

senses.title: Highly strung and quick to react
senses.definition: easily excited or upset, reacting strongly to small things
senses.definitionCN: 容易兴奋或不安，对小事反应强烈
senses.example: The nervous dog hid under the table when the doorbell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 门铃一响，那只见人易惊的狗就躲到了桌子底下。
senses.why: An animal with fine, quick reactions is described as loosely strung rather than steady, so the same anatomical word moved from the wiring of the body to the temperament of a person or animal.
senses.whyCN: 反应细密而迅捷的动物，被形容为绳弦调得过松、不够稳当；于是同一个解剖词从身体的线路上，移到了人或动物的性情上。

intro.en: Nervous is the Latin adjective of sinew, which English first used for strong bodies and later for bodies whose nerves react too quickly.
intro.cn: nervous 是拉丁语中表示「筋」的形容词，英语先用它形容强壮的身体，后来才用它形容神经反应过快的人。

items.en: Nervus meant sinew, tendon or cord, the visible thread running through flesh and bone.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、肌腱或细索，也就是穿过血肉与骨骼的可见细线。

items.en: Nervosus meant full of sinew, strong and vigorous, and it is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: nervosus 意为多筋的、强壮的、有力的，是英语这个形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French nerveux kept the sense of strong and sinewy and passed the adjective into English with its spelling reshaped.
items.cn: 古法语 nerveux 保留「强壮、多筋」的意思，把形容词传入英语，拼写也做了改写。

items.en: English first praised nervous strength in bodies and writing; by the eighteenth century the word had moved to people whose nerves reacted too sharply.
items.cn: 英语最初用 nervous 称赞身体与文章中的强劲；到十八世纪，这个词转向形容神经反应过于敏锐的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the anatomical sense beside the everyday one of worry, and applies the word to people, animals and situations alike.
items.cn: 现代英语把解剖义与日常的担忧义并排保留，并且把人、动物与处境都用这个词来形容。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the noun, adverb, abstract noun and informal adjective of the same family; the near-meaning group holds words for tension and low-level fear.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的名称、副词、抽象名词与口语形容词；近义组收表示紧绷与轻微恐惧的词。

entries.definition: The fibre itself, and also courage or boldness, the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 纤维本身，也指勇气或放肆，是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: In an anxious manner, made by adding -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以焦虑的方式；加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being anxious, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑的状态；由 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Anxious in British use, but bold in American use, made with -y.
entries.definitionCN: 英式指紧张不安，美式却指有胆量；由 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Worried about something uncertain, often with a sense of dread.
entries.definitionCN: 对不确定之事担忧，常带一点恐惧。

entries.definition: Tight and strained, used of muscles, situations and people alike.
entries.definitionCN: 绷紧、吃力的，可用于肌肉、局面与人。

entries.definition: Unable to keep still because of nerves, especially before an event.
entries.definitionCN: 因紧张而静不下来，尤指事情发生之前。

entries.definition: Slightly worried or uncomfortable, milder than nervous.
entries.definitionCN: 略有担忧或不舒服，语气比 nervous 轻。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of sinew, and its senses keep the same taut thread, read first as strength, then as sensitivity, then as worry.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「筋」的形容词，各义项保留同一根绷紧的线，先读作力量，再读作敏感，最后读作担忧。

normal.en: Nervous is built on nerve with the Latin ending -ous, so its literal shape is full of sinew.
normal.cn: nervous 由 nerve 加拉丁词尾 -ous 构成，字面形状就是「充满筋腱」。

normal.en: That literal sense praised strength, which is why older writing can call a vigorous style nervous.
normal.cn: 这个字面义曾用来称赞力量，所以较旧的文字会用 nervous 形容有劲的文风。

normal.en: The modern sense reversed the praise: a body whose nerves are too responsive is easily unsettled.
normal.cn: 现代义把这种称赞反了过来：神经反应过于灵敏的身体容易受扰。

normal.en: The anatomical sense survives in fixed phrases such as nervous system and nervous tissue.
normal.cn: 解剖义留在 nervous system、nervous tissue 这类固定搭配里。

normal.en: Nervously and nervousness simply add the manner and the state to the same adjective, so the family grows without a new root.
normal.cn: nervously 与 nervousness 只是给同一形容词加上方式与状态，词族因此不必另换词根。

abstract.en: A word for strong sinew becomes a word for fragile nerves, because the same thread can be praised as taut or blamed as over-sensitive.
abstract.cn: 一个指强健筋腱的词变成了指脆弱神经的词，因为同一根线既可以被赞为绷得紧，也可以被怪为过于敏感。

abstract.en: Standing before a closed door is the perfect picture of nervousness: the body is ready before it knows what will happen.
abstract.cn: 站在一扇关着的门前，是紧张最贴切的画面：身体在知道会发生什么之前就已经准备好了。

abstract.en: English lets one adjective cover the wiring of the body and the worry of the mind, which is how close the two have always been.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个形容词同时覆盖身体的线路与心里的担忧，可见这两者从来就很近。

examples.en: She gets nervous whenever she speaks in public.
examples.cn: 她每次当众讲话都会紧张。

examples.en: The nervous system controls how the body reacts.
examples.cn: 神经系统控制身体如何反应。

examples.en: He gave a nervous laugh and looked away.
examples.cn: 他局促地笑了一声，把目光移开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢维斯」——神经像细线一样绷紧，人就坐立不安；nervous 就是紧张的。

root: 由 nerve（神经，源自拉丁语 nervus「筋」）加形容词词尾 -ous 构成；本义「多筋的、强壮的」，十八世纪起转指「神经敏感的、紧张的」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a taut cord; it yields the anatomical sense, the temperament of quick reactions, and the everyday feeling of anxiety.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一根绷紧的索；由此长出解剖义、反应迅捷的性情，以及日常的焦虑感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a girl at an exam room door, pressing her cuff again and again while watching the closed door.
core.cn: 核心意象：考场门口，一个女生一遍遍捏着袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的门。

branches.cn: 口试之前的走廊

branches.en: a speaker gripping the lectern
branches.cn: 抓紧讲台的演讲者

branches.cn: 玻璃片上的神经组织

branches.cn: 听见门铃就躲起来的狗

branches.cn: 停不下来的双手

intro.en: The word is a Latin sinew noun, its adjective of strength, the French form that carried it, and the English endings that turn it into adverb and abstract noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「筋」名词、表示强壮的形容词、承载它的法语形式，以及把它变成副词与抽象名词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the sinew noun and the adjective of strength, and the anatomical sense has stayed beside the emotional one ever since.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「筋」名词与表示强壮的形容词，从此解剖义就一直与情绪义并排存在。
